1-1-1.text: This game is played by two players in a match against each other.

1-2-1.text: When a player meets the victory conditions, they win the game.

1-2-2.text: The game will end when one of the players wins or loses.

1-2-3-1.text: When an attack by your Digimon allows for 1 or more security checks, the attack is successful against your opponent, and your opponent has 0 security cards. (For details, refer to 11-5 "Confirming if an Attack is Successful")11-5

1-2-3-2.text: Your opponent has 0 cards in their deck and can't draw a card during your opponent's draw phase.

1-2-4.text: At any point during the game, either player may declare that they forfeit. After a player declares a forfeit, they immediately lose the game.

1-2-5.text: A forfeit is never forced, and effects don't trigger or activate for loss by forfeit.

1-2-6.text: Some card effects can cause a player to win or lose the game. When such an effect is resolved, the player will win or lose.

1-3-1.text: Any card text that conflicts with the Official Rules will be prioritized over the rules. (Example: A Digimon can't attack the turn it's played according to the rules, but a Digimon with <Rush> can attack by that effect.)

1-3-10.text: When cards are to be shuffled by a rule or an effect, you must randomize the order of those cards. If a card to be shuffled is public, it is made private before shuffling.

1-3-11.text: Rules for Declaring Utilization of a Card

1-3-11-1.text: A player can declare they are utilizing a card (playing, digivolving, using, or linking) only if that card is able to be utilized. They can't declare its utilization if they can't pay its cost or alternate cost.

1-3-11-2.text: If processing conditions exist as part of an alternate cost, the player can declare that card only if the processing conditions are currently met and the alternate cost can be paid. (Example: If a card has a play cost of 12 and the effect "When this card would be played, if you have an [Iliad] trait Tamer, reduce the cost by 5," then you can declare you are playing that card if you have an [Iliad] trait Tamer and are able to pay the cost of 7.)

1-3-11-3.text: If optional processing conditions exist as part of an alternate cost, the player can declare that card only if those processing conditions are met and the alternate cost can be paid. Additionally, the player must perform as much of the processing as needed in order to pay the cost. (Example: If a card has a play cost of 11 and the effect "When this card would be played, by suspending 2 of your Digimon, reduce the cost by 4," and you have 2 Digimon that can be suspended and are able to pay the cost of 7, then you must suspend those 2 Digimon if you declare you are playing it.)

1-3-11-4.text: If a card has DigiXros or Assembly, the player can declare that card only if the alternate cost can be paid, including any immediate-type effects (triggered by the declaration of that card) which increase the areas that cards can be placed from. Additionally, the player must perform as much of the processing as needed in order to pay the cost.

1-3-2.text: If a player is requested to perform an impossible action, that action will not be carried out. If only some of those actions are impossible, the player performs as many of the required actions as possible.

1-3-3.text: If a card in a given state is requested to be changed to that same state, the card remains in its current state. (Example: If a suspended Digimon is chosen for an "[On Play] Suspend 1 of your opponent's Digimon" effect, the action of suspending it isn't performed.)

1-3-4.text: If processing is to be performed 0 or fewer times due to a rule or effect, that processing can't be performed. The opposite of the processing can't be performed, even if processing is to be performed a negative number of times.

1-3-5.text: If multiple players are simultaneously requested to make a choice due to a rule or effect, the turn player makes their choice first. After the turn player makes their choice, the2 non-turn player makes their choice.

1-3-6.text: When choosing cards by a rule or an effect, 1 or more cards must be chosen. You can't choose less than 1 card. (Example: "[Main] Choose any number of your opponent's Digimon whose total DP adds up to 8000 or less and delete all of them" would require you to choose at least 1 of your opponent's Digimon whose total DP adds up to 8000 or less.)

1-3-7.text: When a rule or effect modifies a numerical value, the result will always be an integer.

1-3-8.text: When a rule or effect modifies a numerical value multiple times, first the modifying value is calculated, then it's applied to the original value. (Example: If both a +3000 DP and -2000 DP are applied to 1 Digimon, the final modifying value of +1000 will be applied to that Digimon.)

1-3-9.text: Even if a cost to be paid becomes a negative value by a rule or effect, the final cost will not be a negative value.

1-4-1-1.text: "Deck" and "Digi-Egg deck" refer to the decks composed of the cards used in the game.

1-4-1-2-1.text: A deck must have exactly 50 cards. It can't have more or less cards.

1-4-1-2-2.text: A deck can include up to 4 copies of a card with the same card number. However, this doesn't apply to rules or effects that place 4 or more cards.

1-4-1-3-1.text: A Digi-Egg deck can have 5 or fewer cards. As long as it has 5 or fewer cards, it can have as many cards as you like, or even 0 cards.

1-4-1-3-2.text: A Digi-Egg deck can include up to 4 copies of a card with the same card number. However, this doesn't apply to rules or effects that place 4 or more cards.

1-4-2-1.text: The memory gauge shows the numbers that represent the memory. One memory gauge is shared between both players during the game.

1-4-2-2.text: 0 on the memory gauge is the center, and it has the numbers 1 through 10 on both the left and the right. The highest number on the memory gauge is 10 on both the left and the right. The memory won't3 exceed 10.

1-4-2-3.text: 0 on the memory gauge is the center, the numbers on the left represent your memory, and the numbers on the right represent your opponent's memory.

1-4-3-1.text: The marker is used to indicate the current memory. One marker is shared between both players.

1-4-4-1.text: Token cards are non-game cards used by effects. You may prepare as many token cards as you like, but you must prepare token cards if your deck or Digi-Egg deck includes a card with an effect that uses tokens. (For details, refer to 4-21 "Tokens")

1-4-4-2.text: Token cards can't be included in a deck or Digi-Egg deck.

1-4-4-3.text: Token cards must be cards that can show their orientation. (For details, refer to 4-11 "Card Orientation")4-13

1-4-4-4.text: When using token cards, players don't have to declare the effect to be used with the token in advance. However, the card information must be written on the token cards to be used.

1-4-4-5.text: A token card can be played even if its card information doesn't include a play cost.

1-4-5.text: Index (Quick Reference Guide for Keyword Effects and Rules)

1-4-5-1.text: The Index is a card that shows the various keyword skills and rules for cards. You can bring as many copies of the Index as you like.

1-4-5-2.text: The Index can't be included in a deck or Digi-Egg deck.

1-4-5-3.text: The Index doesn't have any effect on games.

1-4-5-4.text: The Index can be confirmed at any point in a game.

1-4-6-1.text: Counter markers can be used to represent various things in the game. Players may bring any number of counter markers.

10-1-1.text: A link is a rule where a card with [Link] can link by plugging it in sideways into one of your specified Digimon on the field according to the link requirements. A card from the hand or battle area can be linked to a Digimon in the battle area by paying the cost as part of the main phase actions. (For details, refer to 6-5 "Main Phase")

10-1-2-1.text: If a card already has stacked cards, the new card is plugged in at the bottom. However, a linked card is not a stacked card.

10-1-2-2.text: A card plugged in sideways for a link becomes a link card. (For details, refer to 4-7 "Link Cards")4-9

10-1-2-3.text: If an immediate-type effect triggers when linking would occur, it will trigger immediately after the card is revealed and the Digimon to be linked is chosen during the link procedure. (For details, refer to 15-8-5 "Immediate-Type Effects")

10-1-3.text: A link is performed using the following procedure.

10-1-3-1.text: The player declares a link and reveals 1 card to link. 1 link requirement is chosen on the revealed card, then the player chooses 1 of their Digimon that meets the requirement.

10-1-3-2.text: The specified link cost is paid.

10-1-3-3.text: The card to link is plugged in sideways into the chosen Digimon, and the link procedure is resolved.22

11-1-1.text: This is a rule where a player can attack a chosen target Digimon in the battle area.

11-1-2.text: Only the turn player can attack.

11-1-3.text: An attack proceeds using the following timings: Attack declaration, counter timing, block timing, confirming if the attack is successful, and the end of the attack.

11-1-4.text: The next timing won't begin until all of the processing is resolved for the current timing. (Example: After declaring an attack, the counter timing won't begin until any triggered [When Attacking] effects and other triggered effects have been resolved.)

11-1-5.note: The rule's example is proven: an attacker that deletes itself on its [When Attacking] still gives the defender the counter timing, the block timing offers no block (12-1-6), nothing checks security and the end of attack timing arrives (attack_timings_continue_when_attacker_leaves_mid_resolution, green since G-ENGINE-ATTACK-TIMINGS-SKIPPED-WHEN-ATTACKER-LEAVES was resolved). Remaining, independent violation: a <Vortex> attack skips the counter and block timings altogether (G-ENGINE-VORTEX-ATTACK-SKIPS-COUNTER-AND-BLOCK, linked through 11-4-1; vortex_attack_has_block_timing, #[ignore]d). Task 13 merged: the Vortex half (vortex_attack_has_block_timing) is proven too, so 11-1-5 is proven in full (controller, at the Task 10 merge).
11-1-5.text: Once an attack declaration has been made, all of the timings that follow will occur. (Example: Even if an attacking Digimon leaves the battle area, the non-turn player's counter timing and block timing will still occur.)

11-2-1.text: The turn player can suspend their Digimon in the battle area and make an attack declaration.

11-2-2.text: At the same time as the attack declaration, the target of attack is chosen. (For details, refer to 11-2-7 "Attack Targets")11-2-7

11-2-3.text: 1 Digimon can perform 1 attack for an attack declaration. Multiple Digimon can't attack at the same time.

11-2-4.text: A new attack declaration can't be made during an attack. (Example: A new attack declaration can't be made using <Blitz> during an attack.)

11-2-5.text: An attack declaration can't be made using a Digimon that can't suspend.

11-2-6.note: The rule's example: [When Attacking] deletes the target; the second opponent Digimon that compacts into its battle-area slot is not battled, the attack fails (no end of battle, no security check). The removal is recorded (PendingAttack::effective_target_removed) and the target is tracked by stack identity, so the slot is never reused (G-ENGINE-REMOVED-ATTACK-TARGET-SLOT-REUSED resolved).
11-2-6.text: Even if the attack target Digimon is removed during an attack, that Digimon remains the attack target, but the attack fails. (Example: Even if an attack target Digimon is deleted by a [When Attacking] effect, that Digimon remains the attack target. The attack fails because the attack target Digimon is removed.)

11-2-7-1.note: At the end of P0's turn a <Vortex> attack is offered against P1's suspended Digimon but not its UNSUSPENDED one (only a suspended Digimon or the opponent is a legal target; <Vortex> adds no target permission, contrast <Execute> 16-38-1). In the Main phase a <Raid> attacker may declare on the opponent or a suspended Digimon, never on an unsuspended one (the highest-DP ones included); <Raid> adds no declaration target.
11-2-7-1.text: When a player makes an attack declaration, they choose either the opponent or 1 of the opponent's suspended Digimon as the attack target.

11-2-7-2.text: After the attack declaration is made and an attack target is chosen, the attack target may switch to another target due to a rule or effect.

11-2-7-3.text: The attack target can't be switched to a target that is already an attack target.

11-2-7-4.text: If an attacking Digimon isn't in the battle area, its attack target can't be changed and its attack won't succeed on any target.

11-2-7-5.text: The processing for switching an attack target may affect the player that made the attack declaration. (Example: It is possible to switch the target of an attack by a Digimon that isn't affected by effects, and it is possible to switch the attack target to a Digimon that isn't affected by effects.)

11-2-7-6.text: If a trigger-type effect with text such as "if attacking XX" will be triggered by an attack, it will only trigger if the attack target chosen during the attack declaration procedure matches the target specified in the effect.

11-2-8.text: The processing for an attack declaration is performed using the following procedure.

11-2-8-1.text: The player makes an attack declaration, suspends 1 of their Digimon to make the attack in the battle area, and chooses an attack target.

11-3-1.text: This is the timing when the [Counter] effect of a non- turn player who is being attacked can activate.

11-3-2.text: During the counter timing, only 1 [Counter] effect can be activated per attack.

11-4-1.note: A <Vortex> attack at the end of P0's turn offers P1 the block timing: P1's <Blocker> blocks and battles instead of the target (the counter timing also opens: combat::counter_interrupt::vortex_attack_has_counter_timing). Ordinary attacks' block timing is proven in ch11_14 (one_block_per_attack et al.).
11-4-1.text: This is the timing when a non-turn player who is being attacked can use their Digimon with <Blocker> to perform a block. (For details, refer to 12 "Blocking")

11-5.text: Confirming if an Attack is Successful

11-5-1.text: This is the timing when confirmation is performed to see if a Digimon's attack on the opponent player or an opponent's Digimon is successful. The following situations are confirmed during this timing.

11-5-1-1.text: The attacked player has 1 or more security cards, the Digimon's attack is on the opponent player, and the attack is successful

11-5-1-1-1.text: In this situation, the attacking Digimon23 will perform a security check on the attacked player. (For details, refer to 13 "Security Checks")13

11-5-1-2.text: The attacked player has 0 security cards, the Digimon's attack is on the opponent player, and the attack is successful

11-5-1-2-1.note: Control: a direct attack on 0 security cards wins; a <Security A. -2> attacker (0 checks) attacking 0 security cards does not win.
11-5-1-2-1.text: In this situation, the player that made the attack declaration wins the game. However, they don't win if the attacking Digimon can't perform any security checks. For details, refer to 1-2-3 "Victory Conditions")1-2-3

11-5-1-3.text: The Digimon's attack is on a Digimon, and the attack is successful

11-5-1-3-1.text: In this situation, a battle occurs between the attacking Digimon and the attacked Digimon. (For details, refer to 14 "Battles")14

11-5-1-4.text: The Digimon's attack is not successful

11-5-1-4-1.note: The target is deleted by the attacker's [When Attacking] (no other opponent Digimon): no battle (no end of battle), no security check, the end of attack timing occurs (EOA_OBS resolves) and the attack ends.
11-5-1-4-1.text: In this situation, no other actions are taken and the end of attack timing occurs.

11-6-1.text: The end of attack timing arrives and the attack ends.

11-6-2.note: While an optional [End of Attack] waits on its decision the attack is still in progress (pending_attack set, AttackState::EndOfAttackDrain) and '+2000 DP for the attack' still applies; once it resolves the attack ends and the DP expires (G-ENGINE-ATTACK-ENDS-BEFORE-END-OF-ATTACK-EFFECTS-RESOLVE resolved).
11-6-2.text: For the end of the attack timing, the attack won't end until all processing has been resolved.

12-1-1.text: A block is a rule that allows a player to switch an attack target to a Digimon with <Blocker> in the battle area. (For details, refer to 16-4 "<Blocker>")16-5

12-1-2.note: Two unsuspended <Blocker>s; after the first blocks, no second block is offered; the blocker battles, the other stays unsuspended, no security check.
12-1-2.text: A block can only be performed once per attack. Multiple Digimon can't block at the same time.

12-1-3.text: A new block declaration can't be made during a block.

12-1-4.note: An unsuspended <Blocker> with '[All Turns] This Digimon can't suspend' is not offered a block (the attack checks security); control: a plain <Blocker> is offered.
12-1-4.text: A block can't be performed using a Digimon that can't suspend.

12-1-5.note: The attacked <Blocker> unsuspends itself when attacked; at the block timing only the other unsuspended <Blocker> is offered.
12-1-5.text: The attack target Digimon can't perform a block.

12-1-6.note: An attacker that deletes itself on its [When Attacking]: P1's unsuspended <Blocker> is not offered a block (no reveal, the blocker stays unsuspended, the end of attack timing arrives); control: an attacker that stays is blocked.
12-1-6.text: A block can only be performed if an attacking Digimon is in the battle area.

12-1-7.text: The processing for a block is performed using the following procedure.

12-1-7-1.text: The player makes a block declaration and suspends 1 of their Digimon in the battle area that will perform the block.

13-1-1.text: A security check is a rule that allows a player to perform a check on the opponent's security stack.

13-1-2.note: A <Piercing> attacker with <Security A. +1> checks 2 cards in its one security check, with one or two <Piercing> instances (see 16-7-5).
13-1-2.text: Only 1 security check can be performed during a single attack. However, if the number of cards that can be checked is modified by an effect on the attacking Digimon, the modified number of cards will be checked in a single security check.

13-1-3.text: A security check is performed one card at a time.

13-1-4.text: If a security check is to be performed, it is mandatory.

13-1-5.note: A <Security A. +1> attacker loses the battle against the first Security Digimon and is deleted: the second card is never checked; control: 2 checks.
13-1-5.text: If the Digimon performing the security check is no longer present in the battle area, that card can't perform any more security checks.

13-1-6.text: A checked card is removed from the security stack and is treated as not being in any particular area.

13-1-7.text: A checked Digimon card is treated as a Security Digimon.

13-1-8.note: Procedure order: the check-triggered effects (13-1-8-2) now resolve before the Security Digimon battle (13-1-8-3), via the §13-1-8 reorder (F2 merge, commit b41f3f5f1). Test is green.
13-1-8.text: A security check is performed using the following procedure.

13-1-8-1-1.text: The top security card is revealed. If the card was already revealed, it remains revealed.

13-1-8-2.text: Processing for effects triggered upon a security check

13-1-8-2-1.note: A defender's 'when your opponent's Digimon checks your security, that Digimon gets -3000 DP for the turn' resolves before the battle: the 7000 DP attacker drops to 4000 and loses to the 5000 DP Security Digimon. Resolved by the §13-1-8 reorder, commit b41f3f5f1.
13-1-8-2-1.text: If an effect is triggered by a security check, that effect is to be resolved. The next action won't begin until all of the processing is resolved for the current action.

13-1-8-3-1.note: The battle happens (see 13-1-5, 16-9-1) after the check-triggered effects resolve. Resolved by the §13-1-8 reorder, commit b41f3f5f1; the citing test is green.
13-1-8-3-1.text: A battle will occur between the Security Digimon and the Digimon that performed the security check. The next action won't begin until all of the processing is resolved for the current action. (For details, refer to 14 "Battles")1424

13-1-8-3-2.note: An Option and a Tamer (neither with a [Security] effect) revealed by the check: no battle (no end of battle, the 1000 DP attacker stays).
13-1-8-3-2.text: If a Security Digimon isn't present, proceed to the next step.

13-1-8-4.note: The revealed Option / Tamer is placed in the trash (not played, its [Main] not activated).
13-1-8-4.text: A card revealed from a security check is placed in the trash unless it belongs to an area.

13-1-8-5.text: If the card performing the security check can perform another security check, it will then perform that security check.

14-1.text: A "battle" refers to comparing the DP of the two battling cards.

14-2.text: The processing for a battle is performed using the following procedure.

14-2-1.note: 7000 vs 3000, 1000 vs 3000 and 5000 vs 5000 DP battles from attacks on suspended Digimon.
14-2-1.text: The DP values of the two battling cards are compared.

14-2-1-1.note: 7000 DP beats 3000 DP; the attacker stays.
14-2-1-1.text: The card with the higher DP is the winner.

14-2-1-2.note: A 1000 DP attacker loses to a 3000 DP Digimon and is deleted.
14-2-1-2.text: The card with the lower DP loses.

14-2-1-3.note: 5000 vs 5000 DP: both lose and both are deleted.
14-2-1-3.text: If both cards have the same DP, both lose the battle.

14-2-2.note: Each loser is in its owner's trash after the battle. Equal DP: both are deleted, and with an [On Deletion] on each both Trash events precede the first [On Deletion] (deleted at the same time, before either effect resolves).
14-2-2.text: The Digimon that loses is immediately deleted. If both lose, both are deleted at the same time.

14-2-3.text: Security Digimon aren't deleted even when they lose a battle.

14-2-4.note: The deleted Digimon's [On Deletion], triggered by the battle, resolves before the end of battle effect; so do the battle-result triggers ('wins a battle'), which pend with it.
14-2-4.text: If an effect is triggered by a battle, that effect is to be resolved. The next action won't begin until all of the processing is resolved for the current action.

14-2-5.note: An '[All Turns] At the end of a battle, gain 1 memory' resolves exactly once after each battle, after the battle-triggered effects (the [On Deletion] and the 'wins a battle' triggers of one pool).
14-2-5.text: If an effect is triggered by the end of the battle timing when a battle ends, that effect is to be resolved.

15-1-1.text: An effect refers to the processing activated by a card that affects the game or cards themselves.

15-1-10.text: If an effect's trigger conditions or processing conditions include a card being added to an area other than the field, the trigger conditions won't be met by a Digi-Egg or token because the card isn't actually placed in that area due to Digi-Egg card or token rules.

15-1-2.note: Ver. 4.3 wording. '[When Attacking] By trashing your top security card, 1 of your opponent's Digimon gets -5000 DP' with two candidate targets: the first prompt is the optional yes/no (security untouched); the OppField target pick comes after it, with the security card already trashed.
15-1-2.text: A single effect is processed in the order shown in the text on the card. However, if that single effect has optional processing conditions that affect it, decide whether or not to perform them before processing the effect.

15-1-3.text: A prohibiting effect takes precedence over an enabling effect. (Example: A Digimon with a "[Your Turn] This Digimon can also attack your opponent's unsuspended Digimon" effect can't attack an unsuspended Digimon with an "[Opponent's Turn] This Digimon can't be attacked" effect.)

15-1-4.text: In some cases, multiple processes will be performed in a single effect. Once all of the processes for such an effect have ended, the effect will be resolved.

15-1-5.text: If an effect is mandatory and not optional, its processing must be performed whenever possible.

15-1-6.text: The processing to execute is chosen, then the processing is executed for the effect. Once the processing to execute is chosen, the effect is considered to be activated.

15-1-7.text: If an effect doesn't specify an area, it means that it can specify or reference a card in the battle area, or that it can affect the battle area. (Example: "[On Play] Delete 1 of your opponent's Digimon with <Blocker>" is an effect where you specify 1 of your opponent's Digimon with <Blocker> in the battle area to be deleted.)

15-1-8.text: Effects that specify or reference Security Digimon can specify, reference, or affect Security Digimon.

15-1-9.text: If an effect's trigger conditions or processing conditions include placing a card in an area other than the field, the conditions will be met even if the card isn't actually placed in that area due to Digi-Egg card or token rules.

15-10-1-1-1.text: If text includes "you" or "your," it affects the player of that card.

15-10-1-2-1.text: If text includes "opponent," it affects the opponent player.

15-10-1-3-1.text: If text includes "players" or "both players," it affects both players.

15-10-2-1.text: If text such as "X Digimon" or "X cards" is written on a card, X number of cards or as many cards up to X as possible must be chosen. The individual processing is performed on those cards. (For details, refer to 15-11-1 "Individual Processing")15-11-1

15-10-2-2.text: If text such as "up to X Digimon" or "up to X cards" is written on a card, up to X number of cards are chosen. The individual processing is performed on those cards. (For details, refer to 15-11-1 "Individual Processing")15-11-1

15-10-2-3.text: When multiple cards are to be chosen at the same time, the same target card can't be chosen multiple times. (Example: If an effect reads "[Main] 3 of your opponent's Digimon get -5000 DP and <Security Attack -1> until the end of their turn," the same Digimon can't be chosen 3 times.)

15-10-2-4-1.text: When "all" is specified, the target cards aren't chosen. Overall processing is performed on those cards. (For details, refer to 15-11-2 "Overall Processing")15- 11-2

15-11-1-1.text: Individual processing refers to when a target is chosen for processing. Individual processing affects the chosen target. This refers to processing where a target is chosen, including text such as "[Main] 1 of your opponent's Digimon gets -7000 DP for the turn."

15-11-1-2.text: If the chosen card for individual processing becomes a new card, that individual processing will be lost. (For details, refer to 3-1-3-1 "New Cards")3-1-3-1

15-11-1-3.text: Individual Processing With Conditions for Choosing a Target

15-11-1-3-1.text: When individual processing has conditions for choosing a target, only a target that meets those conditions can be chosen. This refers to processing with conditions for choosing a target including effects such as "[Main] Choose 1 of your opponent's Digimon with no digivolution cards. That Digimon can't attack or block until the end of your opponent's next turn."

15-11-1-3-2.text: When a target is affected by an effect where individual processing has conditions for choosing a target, the effect will continue affecting the target, even if the target no longer meets the conditions after being affected. (Example: If a Digimon is affected by an effect such as "[Main] Choose 1 of your opponent's Digimon with no digivolution cards. That Digimon can't attack or block until the end of your opponent's next turn," that Digimon can't attack even if it later gets a digivolution card.)

15-11-2-1.text: Overall processing refers to when a target isn't chosen for processing. Overall processing affects cards overall. This refers to processing where a target isn't chosen, including effects with text such as "[On Play] [When Digivolving] All of your opponent's Digimon get -5000 DP for the turn."

15-11-2-2.text: Overall processing that is continuous will also affect targets that are added later. (Example: If an effect reads "[When Digivolving] [On Deletion] All of your opponent's Digimon get -5000 DP for the turn," Digimon placed in the battle area after this effect activates will also get -5000 DP.)

15-11-2-3.text: Overall Processing With Conditions for Affecting Targets

15-11-2-3-1.text: When overall processing has conditions for affecting targets, the processing affects all of the targets that meet those conditions. This refers to processing with conditions for affecting targets including effects such31 as "[All Turns] None of your opponent's Digimon with no digivolution cards can attack or block."

15-11-2-3-2.text: When overall processing has conditions for affecting targets, as soon as a target no longer meets the conditions after being affected, the processing will no longer affect that target. (Example: While an effect that reads "[All Turns] None of your opponent's Digimon with no digivolution cards can attack or block" is activated, an opponent's Digimon with no digivolution cards can't attack or block, but if it later gets a digivolution card, it will then be able to attack or block.)

15-11-2-3-3.text: When overall processing has conditions for affecting targets, as soon as a target that wasn't affected meets the conditions, the processing will affect that target. (Example: While an effect that reads "[All Turns] None of your opponent's Digimon with no digivolution cards can attack or block" is activated, an opponent's Digimon with digivolution cards can attack or block, but if it later has no digivolution cards, it will no longer be able to attack or block.)

15-12.text: Effects That Add Information and Effects That Change Information

15-12-1-1.text: "Effects that add information" refers to effects that add information to a card. These include effects such as "[Main] [Once Per Turn] 1 of your [Marcus Damon] is treated as a 3000 DP Digimon that can't digivolve for the turn."

15-12-1-2.text: Effects that add information can also add information that a card didn't already have.

15-12-1-3.text: An effect that adds information can only add to the play cost, level, or DP of 1 card at a time. If an effect adds information to a card that already has such information, the newly added information will overwrite the previous information. An effect that adds information can only add to the play cost, level, or DP of 1 card at a time. If an effect adds information to a card that already has such information, the newly added information will overwrite the previous information. However, if the same information has already been added by a persistent effect, that effect will always overwrite the information. If the persistent effect is lost, the information will return to the previous state.

15-12-1-4.text: If an effect that adds information treats a card as a Digimon, the rules for Digimon will also apply to that card. (For details, refer to 4-2 "Digimon")4-3

15-12-1-5.text: If an effect that adds information adds DP to a card that didn't originally have DP, the added DP will be treated as that card's original DP.

15-12-1-6.text: If an effect that adds information causes a card to be treated as both a Digimon and a Tamer card, an effect activated by that card will be considered both a Digimon effect and a Tamer effect. (Example: When an "[All Turns] Your opponent can't gain memory other than by Tamer effects" effect is activated, the effects of a Tamer that is also treated as a Digimon will still be considered to be Tamer effects, therefore its effects can still gain memory.)

15-12-2-1.text: "Effects that change information" refers to effects that change the information on a card. These include effects such as "[Security] Change the original name of 1 of your opponent's Digimon to [Sukamon] (white/3000 DP) until the end of your turn."

15-12-2-2.text: Effects that change information can't change information that a card didn't originally have.

15-12-2-3.text: If an effect changes information on a card that has already been affected by an effect that changes information, the most recently changed information will overwrite the previous information. However, if the same information is changed by a persistent effect, that effect will always overwrite the information. If the persistent effect is lost, the information will return to the previous state.32

15-13-1.text: Some effects can be gained through other effects.

15-13-2.text: When an effect is gained, the effect and the state of the effect at that time will be carried over, even if a card is placed on top of that card or a card is removed from its stack.

15-13-3.text: If the gained effect is triggered by the card itself being deleted, that effect's state will be carried over even after being placed into the trash by deletion. (Example: If a Digimon gaining an [On Deletion] effect from an effect is deleted, that gained [On Deletion] effect becomes pending activation even if it is placed into the trash.)

15-14-1-1.text: [X Per Turn] means that an effect can be activated a number of times during 1 turn as specified by X, and each activation counts toward 1 use of X.

15-14-1-2.text: If an [X Per Turn] effect is used X number of times during 1 turn, it won't trigger again during that turn.

15-14-1-3.text: The uses of an [X Per Turn] effect are counted individually for each copy of a card.

15-14-1-4.text: When a player chooses to activate an [X Per Turn] effect, it will count toward 1 use of [X Per Turn], even if the effect's processing can't be executed.

15-14-1-5.text: The number of uses for an [X Per Turn] effect will be reset in the following circumstances.

15-14-1-5-2.text: The card with that effect is considered to become a new card. (For details, refer to 3- 1-3-1 "New Cards")

15-14-2-1.text: An effect with the {Hand} icon can be activated when you reveal the card with the effect from your hand.

15-14-3-1.text: An effect with the {Trash} icon can trigger and activate while the card with the effect is in your trash.

15-14-4-1.text: An effect with the {Breeding} icon can trigger and activate while the card with the effect is in the breeding area.

15-14-5-1.text: An effect with the {Security} icon can trigger and activate while the card with the effect is placed face-up in the security stack.

15-15-1-1.text: If an attack is ended by an effect, the end of attack timing comes immediately after the processing for that effect.

15-15-2-1.text: "Gains" means that a target card gains an effect.

15-15-2-2.text: When a target gains an effect, it is affected by that effect.

15-15-3-1.text: A card being revealed isn't considered to cause the number of cards in its original area to increase or decrease. However, a card can't be referenced as a card in its original area while it's being revealed. (Example: Even if a card is revealed from a security stack, "when a card is removed from your security stack" effects don't trigger. In addition, even if cards revealed from a deck are trashed, they aren't treated as being trashed from the deck.)

15-15-3-2.text: If the number of cards being revealed increases or decreases, then the number of cards in the original area is considered to be modified. (Example: When cards are revealed from a security stack, then one or more of the revealed cards are trashed, "when a card is removed from your security stack" effects will trigger.)

15-15-3-3.text: Another effect can't increase the number of cards in a single area while all of those cards are revealed.

15-15-3-4.text: Until all of the revealed cards are placed into an area, the processing for revealing cards is considered a single process. (Example: If an effect reads "[On Play] Reveal the top 5 cards of your deck. Add 1 Tamer card among them to your hand.33 Return the rest to the bottom of the deck," once the remaining cards have been placed at the bottom of the deck, that text is considered resolved as a single process.)

15-15-3-5.text: If a player is to draw a card during processing for revealing a card from the deck, they draw from the unrevealed cards. (Example: When "[When Attacking] Reveal the top 3 cards of your deck. This Digimon may digivolve into 1 green level 6 Digimon card among them without paying the cost. Place the remaining cards at the bottom of your deck in any order" is used to digivolve, the bonus draw for digivolution is taken from the unrevealed cards of your deck.)

15-15-3-6.text: When returning multiple revealed cards to their original state, the player who owns the card that caused the action to be performed is the player who chooses the order in which the cards are returned. (Example: If an effect reads "[On Play] Reveal the top 4 cards of your deck. Add 1 card with [Gammamon] in its text among them to your hand. Return the rest to the bottom of the deck," is used to return multiple cards to the deck at the same time, the player who activated this effect chooses the order in which the cards are placed at the bottom of the deck.)

15-15-3-7.text: Effects that reveal cards have 2 types: "Reveal" and "search"/"look at."

15-15-3-8-1.text: "Revealing" one or more cards means to reveal them to both players.

15-15-3-9-1.text: "Searching" an area or "looking at" certain cards refers to cards that are only revealed to a specific player.

15-15-3-9-2.text: If a player isn't specified in text, only the player that activated the effect searches/looks at the cards. However, when searching/looking at cards in the hand, they are revealed to both their owner and the player who is searching/looking at them.

15-15-3-9-3.text: After searching an area or looking at cards, the cards are returned according to the rules for the respective area. If searching/looking at is followed by processing, perform it after the cards are returned.

15-15-4.text: Effects that add or reduce an effect's numerical value

15-15-4-1.text: An effect that adds to the numerical value of an effect will add to the value shown in text.

15-15-4-2.text: An effect that reduces the numerical value of an effect will reduce the value shown in text.

15-15-4-3.text: Effects that add or reduce an effect's numerical value can't add or reduce a numerical value that isn't shown in text for an effect. (Example: A "[Your Turn] Add 1000 to the maximum your DP- based deletion effects can delete" effect can't add to the maximum of a "[When Attacking] Delete 1 of your opponent's Digimon with DP less than or equal to this Digimon's DP" effect.

15-15-5.note: Heading '"Isn't affected by effects" cards'; its obligations are 15-15-5-1..4 (ch15_15_unaffected).

15-15-5-1.note: Scope matrix: an opponent-Digimon-effect immunity (Atratusmon ST23-09 idiom) is affected by Option [Main] and [Security]-activated [Main] effects, Tamer effects and its own controller's effects, not by opponent Digimon effects; a full opponent-effect immunity (Magnamon (X Antibody) BT16-102 idiom) blocks opponent Option ([Main] and [Security]), Tamer, Digimon and token effects but not its own controller's; battles and the 0-DP rule check are not effects (Q6279). An immunity that starts mid-effect covers that effect's later steps; one that starts after a -DP effect stops it affecting the card (Q6178; read-time suppression in ModifierRegistry::get). Update (2026-10-17): a keyword gained BEFORE the immunity stops being had when it starts (Q6178), and an opponent's live formula aura stops reaching the card (G-ENGINE-PROGRESS-SHIELD-BYPASSED-BY-TIMING-DISABLE-AND-FORMULA-AURAS resolved).
15-15-5-1.text: When a card isn't affected by effects, it won't be affected by processing caused by effects. (Example: Even if a card that isn't affected by effects is chosen for an "[On Play] Suspend 1 of your opponent's Digimon" effect, it isn't suspended.)

15-15-5-2.note: Record-and-suppress (2026-10-16): a modifier applied to an immune card is recorded (ModifierEntry::affecting_source_kind) and hidden while a covering CannotBeAffected entry exists; it applies as soon as the immunity lapses (the rule's 'while suspended' example: -3000 DP applies on unsuspend) or expires (Atratusmon shape, Q831), for the rest of its own duration. Previously EffectContext::add_modifier skipped the install, so the effect never applied. <Progress> (2026-10-17): an opponent's -3000 DP hidden while the attacker has <Progress> applies the moment it loses <Progress> mid-attack (it battles at 3000 DP and loses), not at the end of the attack; the hidden -3000 DP on the attacker never moves to the Digimon that slides into its slot. Update (2026-10-17): the same for a gained keyword (registry grant) and for a live FORMULA aura (summed inside effective_dp, no stored entry): both apply again the moment the immunity lapses or the attack ends.
15-15-5-2.text: When a card isn't affected by effects, then it can be affected again, effects will immediately start affecting that card. (Example: When a -3000 DP effect is applied to a suspended Digimon with an "[All Turns] While this Digimon is suspended, this Digimon isn't affected by the effects of your opponent's Digimon" effect, the Digimon will get - 3000 DP as soon as it's unsuspended.)

15-15-5-3.note: An immune Digimon is offered by an opponent's 'choose 1' (beside another Digimon, and as the only candidate), can be chosen, and is not affected (Q6176, Q3788).
15-15-5-3.text: "Isn't affected by effects" cards can still be chosen for effects. (Example: A card that isn't affected by effects can be chosen for an "[On Play] Suspend 1 of your opponent's Digimon" effect, but it isn't affected by that effect and it isn't suspended.)

15-15-5-4.note: A <Security A. -1> gained from an opponent's Digimon effect while immune is not counted (1 check); once the immunity ends with the grant still in its duration the Digimon checks 0 cards (Q6179). A granted '[End of Your Turn] Delete this Digimon' (EX6-057 idiom) given while immune activates at the end of the carrier's next turn once the immunity has ended (Q2120 / Q3871). Covers modifier-backed gains (the production SecurityAttackChange idiom) and granted triggered effects; keyword-registry grants (grant_keyword; no authored opponent-side use, reachable only under an own-effect immunity) are still an install-time skip in both directions -- a keyword gained while immune is lost, and one gained BEFORE the immunity keeps applying through it, against Q6178 -- non-blocking (G-ENGINE-UNAFFECTED-KEYWORD-GRANT-INSTALL-SKIP). Update (2026-10-17): keyword-registry grants (grant_keyword) are now recorded and read-time gated exactly like modifiers (KeywordEntry::affecting_source_kind; G-ENGINE-UNAFFECTED-KEYWORD-GRANT-INSTALL-SKIP resolved): a <Security A. -1> gained as a KEYWORD while immune is not had (1 check) and is had once the immunity ends (0 checks); one an opponent granted to a <Progress> attacker is not had while it attacks (§16-39-1).
15-15-5-4.text: Even if a Digimon that isn't affected by effects gains an effect, the Digimon won't be considered to34 have that effect. (Example: If an effect reads "[On Play] 1 of your opponent's Digimon gains <Security A. -1> until the end of their turn," even if a Digimon that isn't affected by effects gains <Security A. -1>, the Digimon won't be considered to have <Security A. -1>.

15-15-6.text: Effects That Can Replace DigiXros Requirements

15-15-6-1.text: Effects that can replace DigiXros requirements allow cards to replace those shown in brackets in the DigiXros requirement text.

15-15-6-2.text: Effects that can replace DigiXros requirements can't replace DigiXros requirements that specify a card that isn't the same as another. (Example: Effects that can replace DigiXros requirements can't replace a card for "∞ Digimon cards w/[Xros Heart] or [Blue Flare] trait & different card numbers.")

15-15-7-1.text: During the processing of effects that activate other effects, another effect will activate and process. (Example: If an effect reads "[When Digivolving] You may place 1 card with [Royal Knight] in its traits and a play cost of 13 or less from your hand or trash under this Digimon as its bottom digivolution card. Activate 1 of that card's [When Digivolving] effects as an effect of this Digimon. Then, <Blitz>," a [When Digivolving] effect on the card placed as the bottom digivolution card will activate, then <Blitz> will be processed after that effect is processed.

15-15-7-2.text: If multiple other effects will activate, the player can activate them one at a time in the order they choose. If multiple types of effects can be activated, choose one and activate it before choosing the next one, and repeat this process the number of times specified. (Example: If "[When Attacking] Activate 1 of the effects below. If you have no other Digimon in play, activate all of the effects below instead" is used to activate all of the other effects, the player can choose their activation order.)

15-15-7-3.text: If an effect that activates another effect has text such as "activate as this card's effect," the card that activated this effect will be considered to have activated the effect.

15-15-7-4.note: Ver. 4.3 rewrite. The DSL expresses borrowing (refire_card_effect, BT15-102 idiom). A mandatory '[When Attacking] Place 1 [Lender] card from your trash under this Digimon; activate 1 of its [On Play] effects as an effect of this Digimon' offers the borrowed 'By trashing your top security card, gain 1 memory' its own optional decision: declining keeps the security card and gains nothing, accepting trashes it and gains 1 memory; a borrowed hand-pick condition keeps its PASS. A refired effect goes through the same optional-decision gate as a lone queued trigger (Game::install_single_trigger_optional_gate, with the §15-7-4 payability guard: an unpayable borrowed condition is not offered, pinned in tests/dsl unpayable_optional_condition). A decline drops only the activated effect: the activating effect's later 'Then, gain 2 memory' still runs (accept: +1 then +2). The parked decision is a resumable-VM frame: two clones of the parked board resolve accept and decline independently and match the original's verification_digest. BT23-060 (the rule's example card) has no behavioural coverage yet.
15-15-7-4.text: Even if the effect activating another effect is mandatory, the player can still choose whether or not to processes that other effect's optional processing conditions. (Example: When activating another effect with the effect "[When Attacking] [Once Per Turn] Activate 1 [On Play] effect on a face-up [Zaxon] trait Digimon card in your security stack as an effect of this Digimon" and that other effect has optional processing conditions, the player can choose whether or not to process them.)

15-16-1.text: Effect timings are shown using text in icons enclosed in brackets.

15-16-10-1.text: [Security] is an effect timing where the effect is triggered at the point when a security check is performed on the card with that effect.

15-16-10-2.note: A revealed Option's '[Security] Gain 1 memory' resolves before the defender's 'when your opponent's Digimon checks your security, gain 1 memory', with no ordering choice offered.
15-16-10-2.text: A triggered [Security] effect will immediately activate without pending activation. Therefore, [Security] effects take precedence for activation even when they trigger simultaneously with other effects.

15-16-11.text: [Start of Your Turn] and [Start of Opponent's Turn]

15-16-11-1.text: [Start of Your Turn] is an effect timing where the effect is triggered at the point when your unsuspend phase has arrived. The effects trigger and activate before the unsuspending actions in the unsuspend phase.

15-16-11-2.text: [Start of Opponent's Turn] is an effect timing where the effect is triggered at the point when your opponent's unsuspend phase has arrived. The effects trigger and activate before the unsuspending actions in the unsuspend phase.

15-16-12.text: [End of Your Turn], [End of Opponent's Turn], and [End of All Turns]

15-16-12-1.text: [End of Your Turn] is an effect timing where the effect is triggered at the point when your turn ends.

15-16-12-2.text: [End of Opponent's Turn] is an effect timing where the effect is triggered at the point when your opponent's turn ends.

15-16-12-3.text: [End of All Turns] is an effect timing where the effect is triggered at the point when a turn ends for all players.

15-16-13.text: [Start of Your Main Phase] and [Start of Opponent's Main Phase]

15-16-13-1.text: [Start of Your Main Phase] is an effect timing where the effect is triggered at the point when your main phase has arrived.

15-16-13-2.text: [Start of Opponent's Main Phase] is an effect timing where the effect is triggered at the point when your opponent's main phase has arrived.

15-16-14-1.text: [Counter] is an effect timing for special activation-type effects. (For details, refer to 11-3 "Counter Timing")

15-16-15-1.text: [End of Attack] is an effect timing where the effect is triggered at the point when the end of the attack arrives after an attack is performed using the card with that effect.

15-16-16-1.text: [When Moving] is an effect timing where the effect is triggered at the point when the card with that effect is moved.

15-16-2-1.text: [On Play] is an effect timing where the effect is triggered at the point when the action of playing a card with that effect is complete.

15-16-3-1.text: [When Digivolving] is an effect timing where the effect is triggered at the point when the action of digivolving into a card with that effect is complete.

15-16-4-1.text: [On Deletion] is an effect timing where the effect is triggered at the point when the card with that effect is deleted.

15-16-5-1.text: [When Attacking] is an effect timing where the effect is triggered at the point when an attack declaration is made for the card with that effect.

15-16-6-1.text: [When Linking] is an effect timing where the effect is triggered at the point when the card with that effect becomes a link card.

15-16-7-1.text: [Main] is an effect timing for activation-type effects. (For details, refer to 15-8-4 "Activation- Type Effects")15-8-4

15-16-8-1.text: [Your Turn] and [Opponent's Turn] are timings where effects can be triggered and activated during the respective turns shown in text.

15-16-9-1.text: [All Turns] is an effect timing where effects can be triggered and activated during both your turns and your opponent's turns.

15-2-1.text: Effects are divided into the following types.

15-2-1-1.note: A token is a Digimon (§4-21-1), so its effect is a Digimon effect: the Familiar Token's [On Deletion] -3000 DP does not affect a Digimon immune to its opponent's Digimon effects (Atratusmon idiom; 12000 DP). Token effects carry EffectSourceKind::Digimon (EffectSourceKind::for_card_kind); Rule is kept for card-less processing only. Attribution witness: effect_source_kind::token_attribution. Update (2026-10-17): still a Digimon effect after the token has left the game -- a YAML token's [On Deletion] that chooses, then applies -3000 DP from a rebuilt context, does not affect the immune Digimon (G-ENGINE-DEPARTED-TOKEN-CONTEXT-FALLS-BACK-TO-RULE resolved).
15-2-1-1.text: An effect activated by a Digimon card, Digimon, or Security Digimon is considered a Digimon effect.

15-2-1-2.text: An effect activated by a Tamer card or Tamer is considered a Tamer effect.

15-2-1-3.text: An effect activated by an Option card is considered an Option card effect.

15-3-1.text: An inherited effect is an effect gained by a Digimon from a digivolution card. This effect can't be activated by just 1 card.

15-3-2.text: An inherited effect gained by a Digimon is considered an effect activated by a Digimon regardless of the digivolution card's card category. Therefore, the effect type for these effects is considered to be Digimon effects.25

15-3-3.text: Even if a card is stacked on top of a Digimon, inherited effects gained by it will be carried over along with their states at that point in time.

15-3-4.text: If "this card" is specified in an inherited effect, that inherited effect is considered to be triggered and activated by that card itself that is or was in digivolution cards.

15-4-1-1.text: Activation refers to an effect being executed.

15-4-1-2.text: When a card activates an effect, all of the effect is resolved, even if that card becomes a new card during the processing for the activated effect. (Example: If your Digimon has "[When Digivolving] Delete 1 of your opponent's Digimon with 8000 DP or less and return 1 of their level 6 or higher Digimon to the bottom of the deck," when you delete 1 of your opponent's Digimon with 8000 DP or less, you will process "return 1 of their level 6 or higher Digimon to the bottom of the deck," even if another immediate-type effect deletes your Digimon.)

15-4-2-1.text: Triggering refers to when the conditions have been met for an effect to trigger. Some effects activate without triggering.

15-4-2-2.text: When an effect's trigger conditions are met during a game, it will trigger no matter the circumstances, even when processing is being performed for a rule or effect.

15-4-2-3.text: Effects that are pending activation must be activated 1 at a time. Multiple triggered effects can't be activated at the same time.

15-4-2-4.note: An observer whose condition is met again before it activates triggers again: one effect's source trash and hand trash give the same Tamer observer two pending entries in one pool, and a third hand trash a third entry; each activates once per fulfilment.
15-4-2-4.text: If an already triggered effect's trigger conditions are met again before it activates, that effect will be triggered again.

15-4-3-1.text: Simultaneous triggering refers to when multiple effects trigger at the same timing.

15-4-3-2.note: <Alliance> and the attacker's [When Attacking] effect pend together in one TriggerOrder before either activates (fire_on_attack enqueues the whole declaration bundle before one drain; G-ENGINE-ALLIANCE-OUTSIDE-TRIGGER-POOL resolved). A battle's 'wins a battle' trigger, the deletion observer and the loser's [On Deletion] pend in one pool: the turn player's TriggerOrder offers its battle-result trigger and its deletion observer together (G-ENGINE-BATTLE-WIN-OBSERVERS-SEQUENCED-AFTER-ON-DELETION resolved). The triggers raised by every event of ONE effect's resolution (a source trash, then a hand trash) pend in one pool when that effect finishes (the batch-window observers are released into the same trigger batch, Game::release_event_window_triggers); a trigger activated from that pool is a resolution of its own, so what it raises pends as a new, derived pool (G-ENGINE-MULTI-EVENT-TRIGGERS-SPLIT-INTO-SUCCESSIVE-POOLS resolved). A return of digivolution cards to the bottom of the deck and a battle performed by an effect raise their triggers inside that effect; they pend in ONE pool with its deck-add trigger when it finishes (G-ENGINE-RESIDUAL-INLINE-DRAINS-OUTSIDE-SOURCE-TRASH, G-ENGINE-EFFECT-BATTLE-DRAIN-RUNS-TRIGGERS-MID-EFFECT resolved). A digivolution's [When Digivolving] and its 'when a Digimon digivolves' observers trigger simultaneously and pend in ONE pool, whether an effect or an immediate replacement digivolved the Digimon. Residual, OPEN (non-blocking): G-ENGINE-OPTION-DISPOSAL-DRAINS-INSIDE-RESOLVING-EFFECT -- the <Delay> disposal of an Option used by a still-resolving effect drains its placement observers inside that effect, so they do not pend in one pool with the effect's other triggers; witness ch15_04_effect_states::option_disposal_triggers_wait_for_the_using_effect is #[ignore]d and fails. `proven` covers the sentence on the paths the listed tests pin, not the Option-disposal path.
15-4-3-2.text: If multiple effects are triggered before a single rule or effect is resolved, they all trigger simultaneously. If effects trigger simultaneously, the effects will be pending activation and activate 1 at a time. (For details, refer to 15-4-4 "Pending Activation")15-4- 4

15-4-3-3.note: The rule's example: an '[Opponent's Turn] -3000 DP' aura leaves a 3000 DP Digimon at 0 DP when its controller's turn starts; its [On Deletion] and a [Start of Your Turn] effect are offered in ONE TriggerOrder, nothing activated before the choice.
15-4-3-3.text: When an effect is triggered by a rule check, it triggers simultaneously with other effects that triggered at that timing. (Example: An [On Deletion] effect on a Digimon that was deleted by its DP becoming 0 at the start of your turn will trigger simultaneously with [Start of Your Turn] effects.)

15-4-3-4.text: The activation order is determined for effects that trigger simultaneously by choosing the next pending activation effect after each effect has been resolved.

15-4-3-5.text: Effects that trigger simultaneously are processed by performing the following procedure.

15-4-3-5-1.note: P0 orders only its own simultaneously triggered attack effects and resolves all of them before the non-turn player chooses. After a battle the turn player's battle-result triggers ('wins a battle', <Piercing>) activate before the non-turn player's [On Deletion] (official Q&A Q3931; G-ENGINE-BATTLE-WIN-OBSERVERS-SEQUENCED-AFTER-ON-DELETION resolved).
15-4-3-5-1.text: The turn player chooses 1 of their effects to activate from among the effects that triggered simultaneously. This step is repeated until there are no more pending activation effects for the turn player.

15-4-3-5-2.note: After the turn player's [When Attacking] effects resolve from their TriggerOrder, the non-turn player orders its 'when an opponent's Digimon attacks' effects (one declaration bundle; G-ENGINE-WHEN-ATTACKING-PARK-DROPS-ALLY-ATTACK-OBSERVERS resolved).
15-4-3-5-2.text: Once there are no more pending activation effects for the turn player, the non-turn player chooses 1 of their effects to activate from among the effects that triggered simultaneously. This step is repeated until there are no more pending activation effects for the non-turn player.

15-4-4-1.text: Pending activation refers to the period until a triggered effect activates.

15-4-4-2.note: Same sentence as 15-4-2-3, restated for pending activation.
15-4-4-2.text: Effects that are pending activation must be activated 1 at a time. Multiple triggered effects can't be activated at the same time.

15-4-4-3.text: When a card with an effect that's pending activation becomes a new card before the effect activates, the effect can no longer be activated. (Example: When an [On Play] effect is triggered by a card being played, if the card is removed from the battle area before the effect is activated, the effect26 can no longer be activated.)

15-4-4-4.text: When a card with an effect that's pending activation loses the effect before it activates, the effect can no longer be activated. (Example: When a Digimon with the text "[When Attacking] <Draw 1>" and "[When Attacking] This Digimon may digivolve into a Digimon card with the [Hybrid] trait in the hand with the digivolution cost reduced by 1" attacks, then it digivolves from the 2nd [When Attacking] effect, the 1st [When Attacking] effect can no longer activate.)

15-4-4-5.note: Trigger-condition qualifier ('When one of your Digimon with 4000 DP or less is played'): a sibling [On Play] raising the played Digimon to 6000 DP first makes the pending observer unable to activate; control ordering activates it. The activation-time re-check is not where a trigger is decided: 'When any of your [TS] trait Digimon win a battle' whose winner had no [TS] never triggers, though a sibling in the battle's pool digivolves the winner into a [TS] Digimon before it would activate (G-ENGINE-BATTLE-RESULT-TRIGGER-CONDITION-NOT-CHECKED-AT-TRIGGER).
15-4-4-5.text: When a card with an effect that's pending activation no longer meets the trigger conditions of that effect before it activates, the effect can no longer be activated.

15-4-5-1.text: Derived triggering refers to an effect that newly triggers while simultaneously triggered effects are still resolving. (For details, refer to 15-8-3 "Trigger-Type Effects")15-8-3

15-4-5-2.text: A derived triggering effect will activate before previously triggered effects that are pending activation.

15-4-5-3.text: If a derived triggering effect occurs for the non- turn player when there are pending activation effects for the turn player, the derived triggering effect will activate first.

15-5-1.text: Trigger conditions are the conditions for an effect to trigger. As soon as the trigger conditions are met, that effect will trigger. Trigger conditions include timings when an effect would trigger such as "when [...] would" text.

15-5-2.note: One 'by trashing 2 bottom face-down cards from under any of your Tamers' condition (BT25-035 shape) trashes its cards as ONE source-trash event after the last Tamer pick: 2 cards from one Tamer -> that Tamer's 'under this Tamer' observer (ST23-13 shape) and the 'under your Tamers' observer each trigger once; 1 card from each of two Tamers -> each Tamer's own observer once, the global one once. Previously each per-card Tamer pick trashed its card as its own event, so every observer triggered once per card (G-ENGINE-MULTI-CARD-COST-TRASH-SPLIT-INTO-PER-CARD-TRIGGER-EVENTS, resolved 2026-10-19). The rule's own security-stack example is not separately pinned here. One return of 2 digivolution cards to the bottom of the deck is one event: a 'when digivolution cards are returned to the bottom of a deck' observer triggers once (the return shares the source-trash event scope; DCGO ReturnToLibraryBottomDigivolutionCardsClass stacks one trigger for the list).
15-5-2.text: A triggering from 1 trigger condition is considered to only trigger once, even if it occurred multiple times at the same time. (Example: An effect that reads "[Opponent's Turn] When a card is removed from your security stack, <De-Digivolve 1> 1 of your opponent's Digimon" will only trigger once, even if 2 or more cards are trashed from your security stack at the same time.)

15-5-3.text: If an effect's trigger conditions are met as soon as a card is placed in an area where they can trigger, that effect will trigger. Example: If a card has a "[Your Turn] [Once Per Turn] When your effect places a digivolution card under this Digimon, gain 1 memory" inherited effect, the trigger conditions will be met even when that card itself is placed in digivolution cards by one of your effects.)

15-6-1.text: When processing has processing conditions, its text will show the conditions for processing the effect. The processing can be executed when those conditions are met. Processing conditions include text such as "if" or "while". (Example: "While this Digimon is suspended" is a processing condition in an "[All Turns] While this Digimon is suspended, this Digimon gets +3000 DP" effect.)

15-6-2.text: A processing condition is a condition for a process to be performed after text such as "if" or "while." Different processes in the same effect don't have to meet the processing conditions for other processes. (Example: If an effect reads "[On Deletion] If you have 1 or fewer Tamers, you may play 1 [Kiriha Aonuma] from your hand without paying the cost. Then, <Save>," <Save> can be processed even if you have 2 or more Tamers.)

15-6-3.note: Same Q1009 witness as 15-8-3-9-2: the second copy's only processing condition is unmet at activation, so it can't be activated.
15-6-3.text: An effect can't be activated when none of its processing conditions are met. (Example: An effect that reads "[When Digivolving] If you don't have [Marcus Damon], you may play 1 [Marcus Damon] from your hand without paying the cost" can't be activated when you have [Marcus Damon] in the battle area.)

15-7-1.note: The rule's example '[On Deletion] By trashing 1 card in the hand, gain 1 memory': an optional hand pick (PASS legal); picking trashes the card and the memory gain follows with no second prompt; declining performs nothing.
15-7-1.text: If an effect has optional processing conditions, its text will show the conditions for processing the effect. If the player chooses to execute the processing for the conditions and is successful, the processing after the conditions is performed. Optional processing conditions include text such as "by X, Y." (Example: If an effect reads "[On Deletion] By trashing 1 card in the hand, gain 1 memory," The "by trashing 1 card in the hand" part is an optional processing condition.

15-7-2.note: The rule's example (trash 2 → unsuspend; After, if [WereGarurumon] in sources, may return a [Garurumon]): declining leaves the Digimon suspended and never offers the 'After' return; control: trashing 2 unsuspends and the return is offered and performed.
15-7-2.text: If the content of the optional processing conditions isn't executed, the processing after the conditions can't be27 executed. (Examples: If an effect reads "[When Digivolving] By trashing 2 cards in your hand, this Digimon unsuspends. After, if [WereGarurumon] or [X Antibody] is in this Digimon's digivolution cards, you may return 1 Digimon card with [Garurumon] or [X Antibody] in its name from your trash to the hand," unless the player trashes 2 cards in their hand, "this Digimon unsuspends" and the content after "After" can't be executed.)

15-7-3.note: The rule's example in BT18-019's production idiom (two sequential trash picks, each returned): with only [Kimeramon] in the trash the condition can be performed only in part, so it is not offered; nothing is returned and [Millenniummon] is not played. Control (both present) passes. The engine gates the leading run of same-zone picks all-or-nothing (leading_cost_guard: one distinct card per pick). Compounds across DIFFERENT step kinds are not composed (gated on the first part only); that stays the DSL by: block, G-DSL-OPTIONAL-PROCESSING-CONDITION-BLOCK (OPEN).
15-7-3.text: It isn't possible to only perform some of the optional processing conditions. (Example: If an effect reads "[On Deletion] By returning 1 [Kimeramon] and 1 [Machinedramon] from your trash to the bottom of the deck, you may play 1 [Millenniummon] from your trash without paying the cost," a player can't just return 1 [Kimeramon] or 1 [Machinedramon] to the bottom of their deck.

15-7-4.note: Ver. 4.3 REVERSED 3.6 (3.6: the player could choose an unpayable condition; 4.3: can't). Owner ruling 2026-10-10 #6. The rule's example with 0 security cards: no optional prompt is offered, the -5000 DP never applies and the 7000 DP defender wins. [Main] mirror: '[Main] By trashing your top security card, <Draw 1>' is masked at 0 security and offered at 1. The engine derives the condition's payability from the clause's leading cost steps (leading_cost_guard: security / memory / suspend / hand and trash pick runs counted per pick / own sources / face-down cards under Tamers / a union-zone pick paid by trash_union_bound, Task 37, read through the pick's own candidate builder) and gates the outer prompt, the pre-cost prompt, the TriggerOrder bundle, the run itself (dropped as if declined), optional replacements and optional cost reducers; the DSL by: block (G-DSL-OPTIONAL-PROCESSING-CONDITION-BLOCK) remains the long-term vocabulary. Update (2026-10-19, Task 40 fix round 2): 'by trashing the bottom face-down card / 2 bottom face-down cards from under any of your Tamers' is payable from every face-down card under your Tamers -- 'the bottom face-down card' is a Tamer's LOWEST face-down card, whether or not face-up cards sit below it (card text BT26-005 / BT25-035 and DCGO BT26_005.cs LastOrDefault(IsFlipped); the PDF is silent; controller ruling). A face-down card over a face-up bottom card is offered and trashed, the face-up card stays; with too few face-down cards nothing is offered. Pinned for both the 1-card and 2-card steps.
15-7-4.text: If executing an optional processing condition's contents isn't possible, then the player can't choose to execute them. (Example: If an effect reads "[When Attacking] By trashing your top security card, 1 of your opponent's Digimon gets -5000 DP for the turn," and the player doesn't have even 1 security card, then they can't choose to execute that condition's contents.)

15-7-5.note: The rule's example: opponent has no Digimon; the decision is still offered, accepting trashes the top security card and nothing else is asked; the attack then proceeds to the security check.
15-7-5.text: A player can choose to execute the content of optional processing conditions, regardless of whether or not the content after the conditions can be executed. (Example: If an effect reads "[When Attacking] By trashing your top security card, 1 of your opponent's Digimon gets - 5000 DP for the turn," a player can choose to trash their top security card even when the opponent doesn't have any Digimon in the battle area.)

15-8-1.text: Effect categories include persistent, trigger-type, activation-type, and immediate-type.

15-8-2-1.text: Persistent effects are constantly activated without being triggered. This refers to effects with text such as "[Your Turn] This Digimon gets +1000 DP" that don't have any particular trigger timings shown.

15-8-2-2.text: Persistent effects are constantly activated as soon as their activation conditions are met. (Examples: If a Tamer card has an effect that reads "[Your Turn] All of your Digimon get +1000 DP," the effect will be constantly activated as soon as your turn begins.)

15-8-2-3.text: Persistent effects won't be activated as soon as their activation conditions are no longer met. (Examples: If a Tamer card has an effect that reads "[Your Turn] All of your Digimon get +1000 DP," the effect will no longer be activated as soon as the opponent's turn begins.)

15-8-2-4.text: When multiple persistent effects are activated, they all overlap.

15-8-2-5.text: If multiple persistent effects with conflicting content are activated, effects that activate afterward take priority, except prohibiting effects.

15-8-2-6-1.text: Persistent effects with processing conditions will be constantly activated while their processing conditions are met.

15-8-2-6-2.text: Persistent effects with processing conditions won't be activated as soon as their processing conditions are no longer met.

15-8-3-1.note: 'When any of your [TS] trait Digimon win a battle, gain 1 memory' triggered by a [TS] winner activates although the loser's [On Deletion] deleted the winner first; control with a winner without [TS] does not (G-ENGINE-BATTLE-WINNER-QUALIFIER-STALE-INDEX). Converse: with a winner without [TS] the effect never triggers, even when a sibling in the battle's pool digivolves the winner into a [TS] Digimon before it would activate (G-ENGINE-BATTLE-RESULT-TRIGGER-CONDITION-NOT-CHECKED-AT-TRIGGER). Every observer timing: 'When your opponent plays a Digimon with 4000 DP or less' (trigger_if:) never triggers on a 6000 DP play, though the played Digimon's own [On Play] lowers it to 4000 DP before the observer would activate; control with a 1000 DP play activates (G-ENGINE-OBSERVER-TRIGGER-QUALIFIER-NOT-CHECKED-AT-TRIGGER).
15-8-3-1.text: A trigger-type effect will always trigger as soon as its trigger conditions are met, then the effect will activate. If an effect reads "[When Attacking] Lose 2 memory" or "[Your Turn] When effects suspend this Digimon, suspend 1 of your opponent's Digimon," that shows a trigger timing.

15-8-3-2.note: Owner ruling 2026-10-10 #1. 'Trash the bottom face-down card from under 1 of your Tamers. Then, gain 1 memory.' with an 'effects trash cards from under your Tamers' observer: the observer waits for the trashing effect's 'Then, gain 1 memory' whether the cause is an Option [Main] or an [On Play] trigger. fire_digivolution_card_trashed no longer drains inline; source-trash observers are enqueued inside a deferred-drain event scope (G-ENGINE-INLINE-DRAIN-SIBLING-TRIGGERS resolved). With that trigger pending, the same effect plays from the trash the very card its cost just trashed from under the Tamer (official Q&A Q6958): the card is placed face-up in the trash (3-6-3) and face-up on the field when played (3-4-2), so the rule check no longer trashes it as a face-down card (17-1-3-2-4) (G-ENGINE-PLAY-FROM-TRASH-OF-JUST-TRASHED-SOURCE-NOT-PLAYED resolved). The direct drains that still ran triggers inside a resolving effect now enqueue only (maybe_drain_effect_queue): a return of digivolution cards to the deck bottom (Zenith BT18-092 shape), the [When Digivolving] of a Digimon an immediate replacement digivolves during the deleting effect (Return to the Primogenitor BT17-097 shape: it activates after that effect's 'Then, gain 1 memory'), and a battle an effect performs (Omnimon: Merciful Mode EX13-077 shape) (G-ENGINE-RESIDUAL-INLINE-DRAINS-OUTSIDE-SOURCE-TRASH, G-ENGINE-EFFECT-BATTLE-DRAIN-RUNS-TRIGGERS-MID-EFFECT resolved). An effect-initiated digivolve's [When Digivolving] and 'when a Digimon digivolves' triggers wait for the digivolving effect's body (DemiMeramon EX13-004 -> FlameWizardmon EX13-029 shape; fire_digivolve_event_triggers enqueues only inside a resolving effect; G-ENGINE-EFFECT-DIGIVOLVE-WD-DRAINS-MID-BODY resolved). Residual, OPEN (non-blocking): G-ENGINE-OPTION-DISPOSAL-DRAINS-INSIDE-RESOLVING-EFFECT -- an Option used by a still-resolving effect (the <Delay> disposal) drains its placement observers directly inside that effect, so they activate before it finishes; witness ch15_04_effect_states::option_disposal_triggers_wait_for_the_using_effect is #[ignore]d and fails. `proven` covers the sentence on the paths the listed tests pin (source trash, deck-bottom return, effect battle, effect and replacement digivolve, resumed effects), not the Option-disposal path.
15-8-3-2.text: Trigger-type effects can't activate during the processing for a rule or effect.

15-8-3-3.text: A trigger-type effect will trigger when the specific conditions are met for the effect on that card to trigger.

15-8-3-4.note: A trigger qualifier (DSL trigger_if:) is decided when the event triggers the effect, at every observer timing (Game::enqueue_triggered -> discard_entries_not_triggered): 'When any of your [TS] trait Digimon win a battle' whose winner had no [TS] never triggers though a pooled sibling digivolves the winner into a [TS] Digimon first; 'When your opponent plays a Digimon with 4000 DP or less' never triggers on a 6000 DP play though its own [On Play] lowers it to 4000 DP first. Processing conditions (condition / active_when) are still read at activation (15-8-3-9-3).
15-8-3-4.text: Trigger-type effects won't trigger when their trigger conditions aren't met.

15-8-3-5.note: Inherited [On Deletion] offered once; pending on the former top card: when the top card's own [On Deletion] returns it from the trash first, the inherited effect can no longer activate (15-4-4-3); control order activates it. DCGO CanActivateOnDeletion requires IsTopCardStillInTrash.
15-8-3-5.text: If a trigger-type effect triggers when a card is deleted, the card where it will be pending activation is the card that was the top card in the original area.28 (Example: Upon the deletion of a Digimon with an inherited effect that reads "[On Deletion] Gain 1 memory" on its digivolution card, that effect will trigger, and it will be pending activation for the card that was the top card of that Digimon.)

15-8-3-6.text: If a trigger-type effect triggers at the end of the turn timing, it will trigger as soon as the end of the turn timing arrives. Once an effect triggers, it will remain triggered, even if the memory increases or decreases.

15-8-3-7.note: Security count read at processing: ordering the sibling <Recovery +1> first makes a level 4 Digimon returnable; ordering the observer first does not.
15-8-3-7.text: If an unspecified reference is to be made during the processing for a trigger-type effect, the reference is made in the state when the processing is being performed. (Example: If an effect reads "[All Turns] [Once Per Turn] When a card is added to your security stack, return 1 of your opponent's Digimon with a level less than or equal to the number of your security cards to the hand," if you have 4 security cards when referencing them for the processing, you would return 1 of your opponent's level 4 or lower Digimon to the hand.)

15-8-3-8.note: The rule's example: the played level 4 Digimon digivolves to level 5 before the observer activates; only the opponent's level 4 Digimon is a legal deletion target. 'When any of your [TS] trait Digimon win a battle' (BT25-020 Marsmon shape): the winner is resolved by identity while on the field (a lower-index Digimon returning first does not redirect the read) and read through its last-known information once the loser's [On Deletion] has deleted it or it has become a new Digimon by DNA digivolution.
15-8-3-8.text: If a reference in the same state as the effect's trigger conditions is to be made during the processing for a trigger-type effect, the state where the effect has triggered will be referenced. The state where the effect has triggered will be referenced, even if the state changes after the effect triggers. This refers to effects where text such as "when another of your Digimon is played" is a trigger condition and a reference is made using text such as "Digimon with a level less than or equal to the played Digimon." (Example: When an effect plays a level 4 Digimon and an effect reads "[All Turns] When an effect plays another of your Digimon, delete 1 of your opponent's Digimon with a level less than or equal to the played Digimon," this effect deletes 1 of your opponent's level 4 or lower Digimon, even if the Digimon digivolves into a level 5 Digimon before this effect activates.)

15-8-3-9-1.note: Two witnesses. The 15-8-3-9-3 example (two branches). Single-branch OBS_OPP_PLAY_GE4 ('if that Digimon is level 4 or higher, gain 1 memory', mandatory): the level 3 play triggers it with the processing condition unmet; digivolved to 4 before activation it activates, otherwise it can't (15-6-3). 'Triggered' is shown through the later activation, not a pending-list entry.
15-8-3-9-1.text: A trigger-type effect with processing conditions will always trigger as soon as its trigger conditions are met, then the effect will activate if the processing conditions are met.

15-8-3-9-2.note: Witness is official Q&A Q1009 (BT2-034: two simultaneously deleted '[On Deletion] If you have 3 or fewer security cards, <Recovery +1 (Deck)>'; the first brings security to 4, so the second's processing condition is not met at activation). Reading of 15-8-3-9-4 (controller ruling, PDF governs): it covers the removed card's own last-known state (its example: 'this Digimon has digivolution cards'); references to general game state such as your security count are made when processing is performed (15-8-3-9-3), which is what Q1009 rules.
15-8-3-9-2.text: Trigger-type effects will trigger if their trigger conditions are met, regardless of whether or not their processing conditions are met. However, the processing conditions must be met at the time of activation in order for the effect to activate.

15-8-3-9-3.note: The rule's example text; control (no digivolve) takes the level 3 <Draw 1> branch. 'When your opponent plays a Digimon, if that Digimon has 4000 DP or less' (condition:) triggers on a 6000 DP play and activates once its own [On Play] has lowered it to 4000 DP: the same board the trigger_if: qualifier decides the other way.
