15-8-3-9-3.text: If a reference is to be made in the processing conditions for a trigger-type effect, the reference is made in the state when the processing is being performed. (Example: If an effect reads "[All Turns] When your opponent plays a Digimon, by suspending this Tamer, if that Digimon is level 4 or higher, gain 1 memory. If it is level 3, <Draw 1>," you will gain 1 memory if your opponent's Digimon is level 4 upon being referenced when this effect activates.)

15-8-3-9-4.note: The rule's example text: deleted with a digivolution card it may play itself from the trash; deleted alone it can't.
15-8-3-9-4.text: If a reference is to be made in the processing conditions for a trigger-type effect that will trigger when a card is removed from an area, the reference is made in the state when the effect triggered. (Example: If an effect reads "[On Deletion] When this Digimon has digivolution cards, you may play this card from your trash without paying the cost," it references whether or not that Digimon has digivolution cards upon deletion.)

15-8-4-1.text: Activation-type effects are effects that can be optionally activated by a player. These include effects with [Main] text such as "[Main] [Once Per Turn] By paying 2 cost, delete 1 of your opponent's Digimon with DP less than or equal to this Digimon’s DP."

15-8-4-2.text: Activation-type effects can be activated during29 your main phase by declaring their activation when there is no unresolved processing.

15-8-4-3-1.text: A player can only declare activation of an activation-type effect while its processing conditions are met.

15-8-4-4.text: Activation-Type Effects With Optional Processing Conditions

15-8-4-4-1.note: Printed <Training> (parsed from the printed text; the DSL grant_keyword: Training clause is declaration-only by design): not in the action mask while suspended; declared while unsuspended, it suspends with no skip prompt and places the deck top face down. General case: '[Main] By trashing your top security card, <Draw 1>' is not in the action mask with 0 security cards and is with 1. The engine derives the [Main]'s leading cost steps' payability (dsl_cards/lower_triggered.rs leading_cost_guard -> Effect::optional_condition_guard; main_effect_select::field_main_match and Game::activate_field_main skip it), alongside the self-cost activation_cost kinds.
15-8-4-4-1.text: If an activation-type effect has optional processing conditions, a player can only declare activation while the optional processing conditions can be performed. In addition, once declared, the optional processing conditions must be performed. (Example: Activation of <Training> can be declared if suspending is possible. Once declared, suspending must be performed.)

15-8-5-1.text: An immediate-type effect will always trigger as soon as its trigger conditions are met, then the effect can be activated. However, these effects will interrupt right before the cause of a rule or effect, unlike trigger-type effects. These include effects with "when X would" or "when X would be removed" in their text, such as "[Your Turn] When this Digimon would digivolve into a card with [Greymon] in its name, reduce the digivolution cost by 1 for each color on that card."

15-8-5-2.text: Activation of immediate-type effects will interrupt right before the cause of such effects. (Example: An immediate-type effect that triggers "when X would be deleted" will trigger immediately before the deletion, and if that "when X would be deleted" effect prevents the card from being removed from the battle area, it isn't deleted.)

15-8-5-3.note: A would-be-deleted effect is offered alone before the deletion; the [On Deletion] of the other simultaneously deleted Digimon triggers after it. Positive half: <Evade> and <Fragment (1)> on one Digimon are offered to their controller as one 'Choose the next immediate replacement effect' choice, and the order chosen decides the outcome (replacement_window.rs install_window_order); G-REPLACEMENT-NO-ORDER-PROMPT no longer reproduces.
15-8-5-3.text: Immediate-type effects will only trigger simultaneously with other immediate-type effects.

15-8-5-4.note: Controller ruling (task 8 review, PDF governs; reverses the earlier [Main]-scope ruling): the cause is the interrupting event, i.e. each 'would be deleted' (15-8-5-1/-2; the example closes the window 'until the deletion is resolved'). Two deletions from one [Main] are two causes: the Sukamon effect activates for each. One-event witness: two non-preventing would-be-deleted effects on one Digimon each activate once in that event, then the deletion proceeds. DCGO enforces neither reading for BT11-041 (ChainActivations -1; IsCutInEffectHasUsed stub). G-ENGINE-IMMEDIATE-ONCE-PER-CAUSE-SCOPED-TO-EVENT retracted. TODO (Task 14, owner-rulings list in qa/rules/mechanics-gaps-2026-10.md): after one immediate-type effect has already prevented a deletion, the engine still offers the carrier's other pending prevention effects in the same window; controller leans engine-correct (15-8-5-1/-5-4/-5-5-2), left unasserted.
15-8-5-4.text: Each immediate-type effect can be activated once until the cause that first interrupted the immediate- type effect is resolved. (Example: If "[Main] Delete 1 of your opponent's Digimon" causes "[All Turns] When this Digimon would be deleted, by deleting 1 other Digimon with [Sukamon] in its name, it isn't deleted" to activate, until the deletion is resolved, the already activated "[All Turns] When this Digimon would be deleted, by deleting 1 other Digimon with [Sukamon] in its name, it isn't deleted" can't activate again.)

15-8-5-5-1.text: An immediate-type effect with processing conditions will always trigger as soon as its trigger conditions are met, then the effect can be activated if its processing conditions are met.

15-8-5-5-2.note: Two would-be-deleted effects on one card: 'if you have 4 or more security cards, it isn't deleted' (unmet at 3) and '<Recovery +1 (Deck)>'; after the recovery the first activates. Control: empty deck, Digimon deleted.
15-8-5-5-2.text: Even if an immediate-type effect with processing conditions triggers when its processing conditions aren't met, it can be activated if its processing conditions are later met.

15-9-1-1.text: Mandatory processing refers to text whose action is required.

15-9-1-2.text: The player must choose to execute the content of mandatory processing. A player can't choose to not execute it.

15-9-2-1.text: Optional processing refers to text whose action is optional.

15-9-2-2.text: The player can choose to execute the content of optional processing.

16-1.note: The bracketed icon <Barrier> parses to the keyword effect; each printed/inherited instance is its own effect: a Digimon with <Barrier> on its top card and an inherited <Barrier> gets an ordering choice, then each instance offered once in one battle deletion (first declined, second accepted).
16-1.text: Keyword effects are effects indicated by icons enclosed in brackets.

16-10-1.note: DIGISORB (<Digisorption -3>, cost 2) from its printed face: digivolving into it from the hand offers <Digisorption> before payment; suspending the base reduces the cost to 0 (never below), and two printed <Digisorption -1> are both offered for one digivolution (Keyword::Digisorption, the digivolve reducer chain).
16-10-1.text: <Digisorption> is a keyword effect. When a digivolution into a Digimon card with this effect in the hand would occur, by suspending 1 of your Digimon, the digivolution cost is reduced according to the value specified in the effect. This is shown on cards using text such as <Digisorption -3>.

16-10-2.note: Offered while DIGISORB is still in the hand, the base still on top and no memory paid (immediate-type, before the digivolution); playing it from the hand offers nothing and pays the play cost.
16-10-2.text: <Digisorption> is an immediate-type effect that triggers when a digivolution into a card with this effect in the hand would occur. (For details, refer to 15-8-5 "Immediate-Type Effects")15-8-5

16-10-3.note: Declining pays the full cost and suspends nothing; once a Digimon is suspended the reduction applies with no further decision.
16-10-3.text: "By suspending 1 of your Digimon" in <Digisorption> is an optional processing condition. If the content of that condition is executed, the processing for "the digivolution cost is reduced" will be mandatory.

16-10-4.note: Two printed <Digisorption -1> on one card: each is offered and paid with its own suspend for the one digivolution (2 - 1 - 1 = 0).
16-10-4.text: If 1 Digimon card has multiple instances of <Digisorption>, they overlap when they trigger.37 Multiple instances of <Digisorption> can be activated for a single digivolution.

16-10-5.note: The suspend candidates include the digivolving base (the Digimon that will become a digivolution card) and the other own Digimon.
16-10-5.text: <Digisorption> can be used to suspend a Digimon that will become a digivolution card.

16-11-1.note: Unsuspended after P1's TurnStart and before P1's PhaseChange into Draw (witness: an inherited 'when this Digimon unsuspends, gain 1 memory').
16-11-1.text: <Reboot> is a keyword effect where a Digimon with this effect is unsuspended during the opponent's unsuspend phase.

16-11-2.note: No decision; an inherited <Reboot> whose source card was removed before the opponent's turn no longer unsuspends the Digimon.
16-11-2.text: <Reboot> is a persistent effect. (For details, refer to 15- 8-2 "Persistent Effects")15-8-2

16-11-3.note: Own + inherited <Reboot>: the 'when this Digimon unsuspends' observer fires once.
16-11-3.text: Even if 1 Digimon has multiple instances of <Reboot>, it is only unsuspended once during the opponent's unsuspend phase.

16-11-5.note: Both the <Reboot> Digimon and the turn player's own suspended Digimon unsuspend in the same unsuspend phase (both observers before the draw phase). The 'no particular order' half has no observable here.
16-11-5.text: The unsuspending from <Reboot> is performed at the same time as the unsuspending of the turn player's Digimon. The unsuspends aren't performed in any particular order.

16-12-1.note: <De-Digivolve 2> on 2 trashable cards parks a non-optional count declaration with exactly the numbers 1 and 2 (count-choice VM, ResumeSelectKind::DeDigivolveCount); declaring 1 trashes the top card only. The trashed top cards fire on_top_card_trashed once per instance, never 'digivolution cards trashed' (4-8-1; DCGO stacks WhenTopCardTrashed only). Resolved G-DEDIGIVOLVE-NO-DECLARATION and G-ENGINE-DEDIGIVOLVE-FIRES-DIGIVOLUTION-CARD-TRASHED. The 'starting with the top card' order is proven by de_digivolve_multi_card_trash_is_simultaneous_but_sequential.
16-12-1.text: <De-Digivolve> is a keyword effect where the player declares a number from 1 up to the number specified in the effect, then the declared number of cards are trashed from the chosen stack(s) of cards starting with the top card. This is shown on cards using text such as <De- Digivolve 1>.

16-12-3.note: Mandatory, nothing to decline, 0 not choosable: <De-Digivolve 1> has no decision, and the 1..N declaration of <De-Digivolve 2> is non-optional with no 0 (G-DEDIGIVOLVE-NO-DECLARATION resolved).
16-12-3.text: The trashing from <De-Digivolve> is mandatory. Once activated, a player can't choose to trash 0 cards.

16-12-4.note: The floor tests the TOP card being trashed: a level 3 Digimon on a level 3 card is not de-digivolved; a level 4 top over a level 3 card stops at the level 3 card (G-ENGINE-DEDIGIVOLVE-LEVEL-FLOOR-READS-NEXT-CARD resolved).
16-12-4.text: <De-Digivolve> can't trash cards from level 3 cards or lower.

16-12-5.note: <De-Digivolve 2>: trash order top first; a 'when the top stacked card of one of your Digimon is trashed' observer (BT21-094 wording; DCGO WhenTopCardTrashed, stacked once per IDegeneration) triggers once. The witness OBS_TOP_TRASH_MEM is authored on the on_top_card_trashed timing (G-DSL-TOP-CARD-TRASHED-TIMING resolved), which the engine fires once per instance with every trashed card.
16-12-5.text: If multiple cards are trashed using 1 instance of <De- Digivolve>, all of the cards are considered to be trashed at the same time, but the procedure for trashing them is 1 card from the stack at a time.

16-12-6.note: With a Tamer card exposed after the 1st card (top category changes), the 2nd card is still trashed.
16-12-6.text: When using <De-Digivolve> to trash multiple cards, even if the category of the top card changes while the trashing is still being performed, the trashing will continue until the declared number is trashed.

16-12-7.note: Two <De-Digivolve 1> instances in one Option [Main]: both cards trashed, and the 'top stacked card trashed' observer triggers once per instance (15-4-2-4, owner ruling 2026-10-10 #5; DCGO runs IDegeneration twice, each stacking WhenTopCardTrashed). The 1st event's trigger used to fail its condition because event_host_is_own_digimon located the host by the top card the 2nd instance trashed; it now locates an OnTopCardTrashed host by stack identity (G-ENGINE-INLINE-DRAIN-SIBLING-TRIGGERS resolved).
16-12-7.text: When separate instances of <De-Digivolve> are executed multiple times in a single effect, the processing is performed separately for each instance.

16-12-8.note: The 1st instance exposes an 'isn't affected by your opponent's effects' card; the 2nd doesn't affect it. Control: a plain card is trashed by the 2nd.
16-12-8.text: When separate instances of <De-Digivolve> are executed multiple times in a single effect, the state of the chosen card is confirmed after each single process for <De-Digivolve> ends. If an effect will be activated as a result of the confirmed state, it is then activated. (Example: When 3 instances of <De-Digivolve 1> are executed in a single effect, if the chosen card becomes an "unaffected by effects" card as a result of the 1st instance of <De-Digivolve 1>, that card is unaffected by the following instances of <De-Digivolve 1>.

16-13-1.note: Deleted as the attack target or as the attacker, <Retaliation> deletes the Digimon it battled.
16-13-1.text: <Retaliation> is a keyword effect where a battled opponent's Digimon is deleted when a Digimon with this effect is deleted in battle.

16-13-2.note: Timing: an effect deletion does not trigger it, a battle deletion does. Kind: <Retaliation> (an OnDeletion effect) and a 'when one of your Digimon is deleted' observer triggered by the same deletion pend in one pool (one flush per deletion batch); P1 orders them through TriggerOrder.
16-13-2.text: <Retaliation> is a trigger-type effect that triggers when just the Digimon with this effect is deleted in battle. (For details, refer to 15-8-3 "Trigger-Type Effects")15-8-3

16-13-3.note: No decision is offered to either player.

16-14-1.text: <Digi-Burst> is a keyword effect where another effect specified by this effect will activate by trashing the specified number of digivolution cards from the Digimon with this effect. This is shown on cards using text such as <Digi-Burst 1>.

16-14-2.note: [Main] <Digi-Burst 1>: activation and PASS both legal; not activatable with no digivolution card.
16-14-2.text: The processing from <Digi-Burst> is optional. For details, refer to 15-6 "Processing Conditions")15-6

16-15-1.note: Played from the hand, a <Rush> Digimon may attack (and does); a plain one played this turn may not.
16-15-1.text: <Rush> is a keyword effect where the Digimon with this effect can also attack in the same turn it was played.

16-15-2.note: A Digimon played this turn gains <Rush> from a Tamer aura ('All of your Digimon gain <Rush>') and may attack at once; no decision.
16-15-2.text: <Rush> is a persistent effect. (For details, refer to 15-8- 2 "Persistent Effects")15-8-2

16-16-1.note: P0 digivolves into a [When Digivolving] <Blitz> Digimon, paying the memory to 1 on P1's side: before the turn can end <Blitz> offers its attack (a ResumeFrame::BlitzAttackDecision prompt; only the attack and PASS legal); the attack checks security, then the turn passes.
16-16-1.text: <Blitz> is a keyword effect where a Digimon with this effect can attack if your opponent has 1 or more memory.

16-16-2.note: <Blitz> is processing of the effect that contains it: ordered after a memory-losing observer in one TriggerOrder, its activation offers the attack inside that effect (only the attack and the decline legal).

16-16-3.note: Opponent memory 1 or more: the attack is offered as an optional decision; P0 may attack (security checked, then the turn ends) or decline (no attack, the turn ends).
16-16-3.text: <Blitz> has a processing condition that requires the memory to be at 1 or more on your opponent's side. "This Digimon may attack" is optional processing.

16-16-4.note: The <Blitz> attack's [When Attacking] gains 2 memory (memory back on P0's side): the declared attack proceeds and checks security.
16-16-4.text: After using <Blitz> to make an attack declaration, the attack will proceed even if the memory moves to 0 or more.38

16-16-5.note: Ordered first, <Blitz> activates at memory 0: no attack is offered, and once the observer moves the memory to P1's side the turn ends; control: the observer first (memory 2 on P1's side), then <Blitz> offers the attack.
16-16-5.text: An attack can't be made using <Blitz> if the memory is at 0 or more upon activating <Blitz>.

16-17-1.note: Activated by trashing the Option, no cost paid, no color requirement (no red card left on the field).
16-17-1.text: <Delay> is a keyword effect. While a card with this effect is in the battle area, by trashing that card, the effect specified in <Delay> will activate.

16-17-2.note: [Main]-activated and [Start of Your Turn] <Delay> both optional (decline keeps the Option). The scheduled half is the conformance pin of G-ENGINE-SCHEDULED-DELAY-MANDATORY-SCAN, resolved 2026-08-24 (73733429d) and moved to qa/resolved-gaps.md.
16-17-2.text: The processing from <Delay> is optional. (For details, refer to 15-7 "Optional Processing Conditions")

16-17-3.text: <Delay> can't be activated the same turn the card with the effect is placed in the battle area.

16-18-1.note: Opponent's deletion effect on another own black Digimon: offered; accepting deletes the <Decoy> Digimon and the other stays. Not offered for a non-specified (red) Digimon, the owner's own effect, or a battle, nor when the opponent deletes their own black Digimon ("your" Digimon only).
16-18-1.text: <Decoy> is a keyword effect. When another of your specified Digimon would be deleted by an opponent's effect, by deleting the Digimon with this effect, <Decoy> prevents the Digimon specified by this effect from being deleted. This is shown on cards using text such as <Decoy (Black)>.

16-18-2.note: Immediate-type: offered while the threatened Digimon is still in the battle area, nothing trashed; it never leaves. Not offered for a return to the hand (not a deletion) or for the <Decoy> Digimon itself.
16-18-2.text: <Decoy> is an immediate-type effect that triggers when another of your Digimon specified by this effect would be deleted by an opponent's effect (For details, refer to 15-8-5 "Immediate-Type Effects")15-8-5

16-18-3.note: Declining: the specified Digimon is deleted. Accepting: <Decoy> is deleted and the prevention follows with no further decision. Matrix row Decoy: optional_cost_then_mandatory, agrees.
16-18-3.text: "By deleting this Digimon" in <Decoy> is an optional processing condition. If the content of that condition is executed, the processing for "<Decoy> prevents the Digimon specified by this effect from being deleted" will be mandatory.

16-19-1.note: Counted toward the obligation: accepting trashes only the top card and the Digimon is not deleted. Not counted: [DCGO-derived, ArmorPurge.cs:13] a lone card (no digivolution card) is not offered; [supporting: §15-13-2 by analogy, §4-7-6] the Digimon keeps a -3000 DP for-the-turn modifier (matrix: surviving modifiers carry over). The 4.3 text says nothing about either.
16-19-1.text: <Armor Purge> is a keyword effect. When a Digimon with <Armor Purge> would be deleted, by trashing the top card of the Digimon with this effect, this effect prevents the deletion.

16-19-2.note: Immediate-type: offered with the stack intact and nothing trashed. Any deletion (effect or battle) triggers it; a return to the hand does not.
16-19-2.text: <Armor Purge> is an immediate-type effect that triggers when the Digimon with this effect would be deleted. (For details, refer to 15-8-5 "Immediate-Type Effects")15-8-5

16-19-3.note: Declining: the whole stack is deleted. Accepting: no further decision. Matrix row ArmorPurge: optional_cost_then_mandatory, agrees.
16-19-3.text: "By trashing the top card of the Digimon" in <Armor Purge> is an optional processing condition. If the content of that condition is executed, the processing for "prevents the deletion" will be mandatory.

16-2.note: A DSL keyword reference without a parameter ('Digimon with <Fragment>', `has_keyword: Fragment`) matches every value of the keyword by type: Keyword::same_type (discriminant equality) + Game::has_keyword_type scan the same origins as has_keyword (modifier grants, face, inherited, adopted, declarative grants, link cards). Proven: <Fragment (1)> and <Fragment (2)> Digimon are both choosable, a Digimon without the keyword is not. Supporting evidence (not counted): the printed icons parse to one Keyword variant per keyword.
16-2.text: A keyword effect is considered to be the same type even if it has a different numerical value or specified card included in the icon enclosed in brackets.

16-20-1.text: <Save> is a keyword effect that allows you to place this card under 1 of your Tamers.

16-20-2.note: <Save> is processed within its own [On Deletion] effect, ordered by the player with another [On Deletion] of the same deletion.

16-21-1.note: Only DigiXros-specified cards from the digivolution cards are offered; not offered on a bounce.
16-21-1.text: <Material Save> is a keyword effect. When a Digimon with this effect is deleted, this effect allows you to place a number of the cards specified in the top card's DigiXros requirements from among the digivolution cards under 1 of your Tamers. The number of cards placed is the number specified in this keyword effect. This is shown on cards using text such as <Material Save 1>.

16-21-2.note: Offered as a non-cancelling 'would be deleted' immediate effect while the Digimon and its digivolution cards are still in the battle area; nothing is in the trash yet.
16-21-2.text: <Material Save> is an immediate-type effect that triggers when the Digimon with this effect would be deleted. (For details, refer to 15-8-5 "Immediate-Type Effects")15-8-5

16-21-3.note: The Tamer pick is the optional decision (declinable); once taken, exactly min(N, specified cards) must be placed: the card pick is not optional until full.
16-21-3.text: The processing from <Material Save> is optional. However, if <Material Save> will be processed, the number of cards specified by this effect must be placed under your Tamer whenever possible.

16-21-4.note: The pick order decides the stacking. The 'considered placed at the same time' half has no observer staged.
16-21-4.text: When multiple cards would be placed under 1 Tamer for 1 instance of <Material Save>, the procedure for placing them is 1 card at a time, but they are considered to be placed at the same time. In addition, the placement order is chosen by the player processing <Material Save>.

16-21-5.text: As long as you use a card specified in the DigiXros requirements, multiple copies of the same card can be placed under the Tamer for <Material Save>. (Example: If a Digimon with <Material Save 2> has [Shoutmon]×[Ballistamon]×[Dorulumon] in its DigiXros requirements, 2 copies of [Shoutmon] can be placed under the Tamer.)

16-21-6.text: If there are any cards stacked under the Tamer when processing <Material Save>, the new card is placed at the bottom.

16-22-1.note: Accepting suspends the Digimon and it is not deleted. Already suspended (suspending isn't performed, 1-3-3, so the condition can't be executed, 15-7-4): not offered.
16-22-1.text: <Evade> is a keyword effect. By suspending a Digimon with this effect when it would be deleted, this effect prevents the deletion.

16-22-2.note: Immediate-type: offered while unsuspended in the battle area, nothing trashed. Triggers for its owner's own effect and for a battle (battle_digimon); not for a return to the hand.
16-22-2.text: <Evade> is an immediate-type effect that triggers when the Digimon with this effect would be deleted. (For39 details, refer to 15-8-5 "Immediate-Type Effects")15-8-5

16-22-3.note: Declining: deleted. Accepting: no further decision. Matrix row Evade: optional_cost_then_mandatory, agrees.
16-22-3.text: "By suspending a Digimon with this effect" in <Evade> is an optional processing condition. If the content of that condition is executed, the processing for "prevents the deletion" will be mandatory.

16-23-1.note: The switch offers only the highest-DP unsuspended Digimon; the attack battles the chosen one and checks nothing. <Raid> SWITCHES after the declaration: it adds no declaration target (an unsuspended Digimon is not offered at declaration), and the switch is offered after a declaration on the opponent or on a suspended Digimon (G-ENGINE-RAID-DECLARATION-TARGET-UNSUSPENDED, resolved).
16-23-1.text: <Raid> is a keyword effect that can switch the target of attack to the opponent's unsuspended Digimon with the highest DP when a Digimon with this keyword effect attacks.

16-23-2.note: Another Digimon's attack offers no <Raid>; <Raid> is a [When Attacking] trigger-type body pending with the attacker's [When Attacking] effect in one TriggerOrder.
16-23-2.text: <Raid> is a trigger-type effect that triggers when a Digimon with this effect attacks. (For details, refer to 15-8-3 "Trigger-Type Effects")15-8-3

16-23-3.note: Declining keeps the attack on the player. Matrix row Raid (optional) agrees.

16-23-4.note: With two tied highest-DP Digimon the attacking player (P0) is offered both and picks one.
16-23-4.text: If the opponent has multiple unsuspended Digimon with the highest DP when <Raid> activates, the player that activated the effect chooses a Digimon from among them and the attack target is switched to it.

16-24-1.note: Only when this Digimon attacks; only another unsuspended own Digimon is offered; the DP lasts for the attack only.
16-24-1.text: <Alliance> is a keyword effect. When a Digimon with this effect attacks, by suspending 1 of your other Digimon, add the suspended Digimon's DP to the attacking Digimon and it gains <Security A. +1> for the attack.

16-24-2.note: <Alliance> is a [When Attacking] trigger-type body (keyword_to_auto_effect) pending with the attack declaration's other triggers; its ally pick is the body.
16-24-2.text: <Alliance> is a trigger-type effect that triggers when a Digimon with this effect attacks. (For details, refer to 15-8-3 "Trigger-Type Effects")15-8-3

16-24-3.note: Declining: no suspension, no DP. Suspending: +DP and <Security A. +1> follow with no further decision. Matrix row Alliance (optional_cost_then_mandatory) agrees.
16-24-3.text: "By suspending 1 of your other Digimon" in <Alliance> is an optional processing condition. If the content of that condition is executed, the processing for "when a Digimon with this effect attacks, by suspending 1 of your other Digimon, add the suspended Digimon's DP to the attacking Digimon and it gains <Security A. +1> for the attack" will be mandatory.

16-24-4.note: A [Counter] -3000 DP on the suspended Digimon leaves the attacker's added DP unchanged.
16-24-4.text: The value added to DP by <Alliance> is the value of the suspended Digimon upon the suspension. The added DP from <Alliance> isn't modified, even if the DP of your suspended Digimon is later modified.

16-24-5.note: A [Counter] deleting the suspended Digimon leaves the added DP and <Security A. +1>.
16-24-5.text: Even if your Digimon that was suspended by <Alliance> is removed from the battle area during the attack, the added DP and <Security A. +1> remain.

16-25-1.note: Battle deletion: accepting trashes the TOP security card and the Digimon survives. Effect deletion: not offered. 0 security cards: not offered (15-7-4).
16-25-1.text: <Barrier> is a keyword effect. When a Digimon with this effect would be deleted in battle, by trashing the top card of your security stack, this effect prevents that deletion.

16-25-2.note: Immediate-type: offered with the Digimon in the battle area and the security stack intact. Triggers for the attacker losing its battle too.
16-25-2.text: <Barrier> is an immediate-type effect that triggers when the Digimon with this effect would be deleted in battle. (For details, refer to 15-8-5 "Immediate-Type Effects")15-8-5

16-25-3.note: Declining: deleted, security untouched. Accepting: the top security card is trashed and no further decision follows. Matrix row Barrier: optional_cost_then_mandatory, agrees.
16-25-3.text: "By trashing the top card of your security stack" in <Barrier> is an optional processing condition. If the content of that condition is executed, the processing for "prevents the deletion" will be mandatory.

16-26-1.text: <Blast Digivolve> is a keyword effect that allows one of your Digimon to digivolve into a card with this keyword effect in the hand without paying the cost.

16-26-3.text: The processing from <Blast Digivolve> is optional.

16-26-4.note: Only the Lv.4 Digimon that can digivolve are offered; the chosen one digivolves, the other is unchanged.
16-26-4.text: <Blast Digivolve> is an effect that digivolves the chosen Digimon in the battle area.

16-27-1.text: <Fortitude> is a keyword effect. When a Digimon with digivolution cards and this effect is deleted, you play this Digimon without paying the cost.

16-27-2.note: Pends in one TriggerOrder with an inherited [On Deletion] of the same deletion; triggers on effect and battle deletion, not on a bounce.
16-27-2.text: <Fortitude> is a trigger-type effect that triggers when a Digimon with digivolution cards and this effect is deleted. (For details, refer to 15-8-3 "Trigger-Type Effects")

16-28-1.note: Only a Digimon with no Tamer card in its digivolution cards can be chosen; not activatable without one.
16-28-1.text: <Mind Link> is a keyword effect that places a Tamer with this effect in the digivolution cards of a Digimon with no Tamer cards in its digivolution cards.

16-28-3.note: The [Main] timing is the player's choice (proven); once activated the Digimon pick is mandatory (is_optional=false, so PASS is not legal) and the Tamer is placed. The rule governs over DCGO's canNoSelect: true.
16-28-3.text: The processing from <Mind Link> is mandatory. However, if it uses the [Main] activation timing, it can be activated and processed at a timing chosen by the player.

16-29-1.note: Opponent's deletion effect: offered; accepting plays the blue Lv.4 and the green Lv.4 for free; with two blue Lv.4 cards exactly one blue and the green are played, the other blue is trashed. Not offered without 1 of each specified card, for the owner's own effect, or in battle. 16-29-1.text: <Partition> is a keyword effect. When a Digimon with40 this effect and 1 of each of the specified cards in its digivolution cards would be removed from the battle area other than by one of your effects or a battle, you may play 1 of each of the specified cards from the digivolution cards without paying their costs. This is shown on cards using text such as "<Partition (blue Lv.4 & green Lv.4)>."

16-29-2.note: Immediate-type: offered with the full stack in the battle area, nothing trashed. Triggers for a return to the hand too (removal, not only deletion). The plays are sequential, not one simultaneous play: G-ENGINE-PARTITION-PLAYS-NOT-SIMULTANEOUS (not asserted here). Holds for cards authored with `kind: partition` + `sources:` (one predicate per slot) + `exclude_cause: [own_effect, battle]`; the synthesized Keyword::Partition body hard-codes the Battle/OwnEffect cause skip. This is the production authoring path (AD1-011, BT16-025, BT20-037). A dsl-lint guard is proposed in qa/dsl-vocab-gaps.md (G-DSL-REPLACEMENT-KEYWORD-EXCLUSIONS-LINT).
16-29-2.text: <Partition> is an immediate-type effect that triggers "when a Digimon with this effect and 1 of each of the specified cards in its digivolution cards would be removed from the battle area other than by one of your effects or a battle." (For details, refer to 15-8-5 "Immediate-Type Effects")15-8-5

16-29-3.note: Declining: nothing played, the stack is deleted. Matrix row Partition: optional, agrees.

16-29-4.note: Once accepted, any card pick the engine asks for can't be declined and both specified cards are always played (1 of each, never 2 blues). The number of picks is not asserted (today's play-order pick is an artifact of G-ENGINE-PARTITION-PLAYS-NOT-SIMULTANEOUS).
16-29-4.text: When <Partition> is activated, 1 of each of the specified cards is played from digivolution cards without paying their costs. A player can't choose to only play one or some of the specified cards.

16-3.text: "Specified cards" for a keyword effect refers to the cards that meet the conditions shown in parentheses for icons that use angle brackets.

16-30-1.note: Both halves proven: has_keyword(h, Blocker) is true for each opponent Digimon during the attack (Game::collision_grants_blocker), and the block window is mandatory. G-ENGINE-COLLISION-BLOCKER-NOT-GRANTED resolved.
16-30-1.text: <Collision> is a keyword effect. While a Digimon with this effect is attacking, all of your opponent's Digimon gain <Blocker> and the opponent player is forced to block whenever possible during the block timing.

16-30-2.note: The grant is persistent and live-computed from the current attack (no activation, no modifier that could outlive it); absent before the attack, present at the block timing.
16-30-2.text: <Collision> is a persistent effect. (For details, refer to 15-8-2 "Persistent Effects")15-8-2

16-30-3.note: Another Digimon's attack forces no block.
16-30-3.text: <Collision> will activate while the Digimon with this effect is attacking.

16-30-4.note: A Digimon unaffected by the attacker's Digimon effects does not gain <Blocker> (effect_can_affect gate) and is not a forced candidate; the forced block still falls on the opponent player.
16-30-4.text: "All of your opponent's Digimon gain <Blocker>" in <Collision> is processing that affects Digimon. "The opponent player is forced to block whenever possible" is processing that affects the opponent player.

16-31-1.text: <Blast DNA Digivolve> is a keyword effect. One of your Digimon specified in this effect and a card from your hand may digivolve into a card with this keyword effect in the hand without paying the cost. This is shown on cards using text such as "<Blast DNA Digivolve> <[Durandamon] + [BryweLudramon]>."

16-31-3.text: The processing from <Blast DNA Digivolve> is optional.

16-31-4.note: One DNA digivolution, stacked per 8-2-2-2, at no cost; a card with no DNA requirement to meet is not offered.
16-31-4.text: <Blast DNA Digivolve> is an effect that performs DNA digivolution. (For details, refer to 8-2 "DNA Digivolution")8-2

16-31-5.note: A same-named level 4 field Digimon (DNA requirement: Lv.5) is not offered; the level 5 control is.
16-31-5.text: A Digimon card's DNA digivolution requirements can't be ignored for <Blast DNA Digivolve>.

16-31-6.note: Witness: the field Digimon and the hand card are both chosen before any card moves (no reveal-from-hand event exists to observe the reveal itself).
16-31-6.text: When DNA digivolution is performed using <Blast DNA Digivolve>, the player reveals the cards that will become digivolution cards from their hand at the same time as when they choose their Digimon that meet the DNA digivolution requirements.

16-32-1.note: Opponent's effect and battle: offered; accepting deletes the other own Digimon and the <Scapegoat> Digimon stays. Owner's own effect: not offered. Staged via the printed-keyword parse (not DSL-grantable).
16-32-1.text: <Scapegoat> is a keyword effect. By deleting 1 of your other Digimon when a Digimon with this effect would be deleted other than by one of your effects, this effect prevents the deletion.

16-32-2.note: Immediate-type: offered while in the battle area, nothing trashed. Not offered for a return to the hand, or with no other own Digimon (15-7-4).
16-32-2.text: <Scapegoat> is an immediate-type effect that triggers when the Digimon with this effect would be deleted other than by one of your effects. (For details, refer to 15-8-5 "Immediate-Type Effects")15-8-5

17-1-2-2.note: The rule's example '[On Play] [When Digivolving] 1 of your opponent's Digimon gets -3000 DP and <Security A. -1>' on a 3000 DP Digimon: at the would-be-deleted decision it is at 0 DP and already has SecurityAttackChange -1, so the effect finished before the rule check deleted it.
17-1-2-2.text: Rule checks aren't performed during effect processing. (Example: If an effect reads "[On Play] [When Digivolving] 1 of your opponent's Digimon gets -3000 DP and <Security Attack -1> until the end of their turn," a Digimon whose DP becomes 0 due to getting -3000 DP will be deleted upon a rule check after it gains <Security A. -1>.)

17-1-3.note: The rule check collects every target first, trashes the trash targets, deletes every 0 DP Digimon in ONE deletion batch and flushes once inside one deferred-drain scope (Game::run_state_based_rules_check): two 0 DP Digimon are both in the trash before their [On Deletion] effects pend together in one TriggerOrder; with an orphan Option and a 0 DP Digimon (both slot orders) the [On Deletion] activates after both removals.
17-1-3.text: The respective processing is performed simultaneously for the following circumstances during timings when rule checks are possible.

17-1-3-1-1.note: -3000 DP on a 3000 DP Digimon: deleted at the rule check (its [On Deletion] activates); control 7000 DP stays at 4000.
17-1-3-1-1.text: A Digimon placed in the battle area whose DP is 0

17-1-3-2-1.note: A Digimon card printed without DP is trashed at the rule check; its [On Deletion] does not activate; a 1000 DP Digimon next to it stays.
17-1-3-2-1.text: Digimon without DP placed in the battle area

17-1-3-2-2.note: An Option in the battle area that no effect placed there is trashed; control: an Option placed by its own '[Main] Place this card in the battle area' (§4-28-1) stays.
17-1-3-2-2.text: Option cards placed in the battle area (except Option cards placed in the battle area by an effect)

17-1-3-2-3.note: A Tamer in the breeding area that no effect placed there is trashed at the rule check; control: a Digimon there stays. The exception reads Permanent::placed_by_effect, set by the effect placement into the breeding area (Game::play_to_breeding_from_hand) and false for a hatched Digi-Egg.
17-1-3-2-3.text: Cards other than Digimon placed in the breeding area (except cards placed in the breeding area by an effect)

17-1-3-2-4.note: Rule-check trash target (normative; explicit so the short text is never read as a heading). A permanent whose TOP card is face down is trashed at the rule check; control: a face-down card stacked under a Tamer stays. The conformance test stages the battle area; the breeding-area case (also part of the field, §3-4-6) is pinned by the lib unit test game_actions::breeding::rule_check_breeding_tests::face_down_top_in_breeding_area_is_trashed_face_up.
17-1-3-2-4.text: Face-down cards placed on the field

17-1-3-2-5.note: A host over its link limit (base 1, §4-9-5) parks its controller's choice of exactly the excess link cards at the rule check (Q6370; one pick per decision, trashed together; when every removable card is excess they are trashed directly). Both the 2-link and 6-link boards are green.
17-1-3-2-5.text: Link cards for a Digimon that has exceeded the link limit (only the cards that exceed link limit are trashed)

17-1-3-2-6.note: The rule check re-evaluates each link card's link requirement against its host (collect_link_rule_targets) and trashes the failures with no choice. A printed Link box whose requirement isn't lowered counts as met (G-DATA-LINK-REQUIREMENT-NOT-LOWERED).
17-1-3-2-6.text: Link cards that don't meet the link requirements

17-1-3-2-7.note: A linked card with no [Link] (so no <Link> note names its category) is trashed by the same per-host link step. The witness is really a 17-1-3-2-6 board (a Tamer card with no link requirement); the category-restricting <Link> note model is not built: no card's <Link> note restricts categories in the engine, so any card with a link requirement passes the category half.
17-1-3-2-7.text: Linked cards in a card category other than those specified in the notes for <Link>

18-1-1.note: The rule's example '[When Attacking] Gain 3 memory. Lose 3 memory at the end of the turn' (schedule_delayed): after the attack only +3 is applied and the turn goes on; on pass the -3 is processed before P1's TurnStart.
18-1-1.text: Pending processing refers to processing for rules or effects that is pending. Pending processing will be processed at the predetermined timing for the corresponding rule or effect, similar to triggered effects. (Example: If an effect reads "[When Attacking] Gain 3 memory. Lose 3 memory at the end of the turn," "lose 3 memory at the end of the turn" is pending processing that is processed similar to how it would be processed if it triggered at the end of the turn.)

18-1-2.note: The 18-1-1 board plus EOT_MEM ([End of Your Turn] Gain 2 memory): at the end of P0's turn the pending -3 and EOT_MEM are offered in ONE TriggerOrder to P0 before either is processed, and both orders are honoured. Every timing site enqueues its due ScheduledEffects (Game::enqueue_scheduled_for_timing) into the same batch as the printed triggers before draining. The provenance-keyed turn-end deletion (delete the Digimon this effect played) pools the same way; an optional effect ordered first keeps its accept/decline; the end-of-opponent's-turn pool resolves before the turn passes (no turn advance or TurnStart while it waits); a pending deletion whose Digimon already left is not offered.
18-1-2.text: If other processing will be performed at the same time as pending processing, it is performed similar to effects that trigger simultaneously. For details, refer to 15-4-3 "Simultaneous Triggering")15-4-3

18-2-1.note: The rule's example Option against 1000/3000/7000 DP: without [Greymon] the deletion is offered on the two 6000-or-less Digimon; with [Greymon] only on the lowest DP one; a lone 7000 DP Digimon is deleted only by the overwriting processing. The DSL author expresses 'instead' with if/else.
18-2-1.text: Overwrite processing refers to when the processing that is normally performed for a rule or effect is overwritten with different processing using "instead" in text. (Example: In an effect that reads "[Main] Delete 1 of your opponent's Digimon with 6000 DP or less. If you have a Digimon with [Greymon] in its name, instead delete 1 of your opponent's Digimon with the lowest DP," the overwrite processing is shown right before "instead."

18-2-2.note: '[On Play] Gain 1 memory. If you have a Tamer, you may <Draw 1> instead.' via select_effect_choice + legal_when: no Tamer, no prompt and +1 memory; with a Tamer the player picks, and each branch performs only its own processing. Expressible in the DSL, so no vocab gap.
18-2-2.text: If overwrite processing is optional, it will be possible to choose to overwrite with the different processing shown for the "instead" in text, and it will be considered optional processing. (Example: If an effect reads "[On Play] Reveal the top 4 cards of your deck. Add 2 cards with the [Blue Flare] trait among them to the hand. Return the rest to the bottom of the deck in any order. When you have [Kiriha Aonuma], you may return 1 [MetalGreymon] from your trash to your hand instead," while the player has [Kiriha Aonuma], they can choose whether or not the processing is replaced with the processing shown for "instead," and they can choose whether or not they return 1 [MetalGreymon] from their trash to the hand.)

18-2-3.note: With the condition met, no choice to keep the normal processing is offered: the first decision is the lowest-DP pick, which excludes the 3000 DP Digimon the normal processing allowed.
18-2-3.text: If overwrite processing is mandatory, the processing must be overwritten with the different processing shown for the "instead" in text, and it will be considered mandatory processing.

18-2-4.text: The overwrite processing for immediate-type effects can't be interrupted. (Example: If an effect reads "when any digivolution card would be trashed from another of your Digimon by effects, you may trash a digivolution card from this Digimon instead," it can't be interrupted.

18-3-1.note: Definition; pinned with 18-3-2. From LOOP_WATCH_START (20) steps on, the drainer records a loop signature (pending entries + board: zones' card handles, suspension, effective DP, per-turn activation counts, memory) before each resolution step; the same state seen LOOP_SIGNATURE_REPEATS (3) times with no declinable decision in between is a loop. A 60-card self-chaining trigger (~120 chained resolutions that end when the deck empties) and a chain whose only progress is DP (+1000 per cycle up to 30000) both run to their end with no loop event.
18-3-1.text: An infinite loop refers to a state where a set of processing will continue infinitely or must be continued infinitely as a result of processing for a rule or effect, and game progress is no longer possible.

18-3-2.note: A mandatory suspend/unsuspend loop: GameEvent::InfiniteLoop then GameOver { winner: None, reason: InfiniteLoopDraw }. Forced decisions do not reset the loop watch, so a loop whose repetitions only ask a mandatory pick (one option or two) or an immediate-replacement order also draws. The draw is final: one declared inside an attack stops the attack (no later security check, no second GameOver; the first terminal outcome stands). MAX_CHAIN_DEPTH (10_000) remains a far backstop that ends in the same draw, counted both on the chain depth and on the loop watch's age (steps since the last optional decision), so a forced-prompt loop whose DP grows without bound also draws; nothing is cleared with the game going on. Update (2026-10-17): the watch now spans outermost drains -- it resets only on a player decision (a declinable prompt, a runner action, end_turn, a declared attack or a play from hand), never when a drain merely settles, so a loop that runs through several drains with no decision between them (an effect-started attack, a re-fired turn-structure trigger) also draws (game::infinite_loop::loop_watch_tests).
18-3-2.text: If an infinite loop occurs and neither player has the ability to stop it, that game ends in a draw.

18-3-3.note: A loop with 'you may suspend it' is offered once per repetition (ruling W10): every resolved declinable decision resets the loop watch and every decision restarts the chain count, so P0 repeats it 40 times, stops it, the Digimon stays unsuspended, the game goes on, and P1's trigger pending since the play activates once. (The test's final MemoryChange expectation was corrected to the turn-player-signed delta -1 by controller ruling; the test had never reached it.) W10 (per-repetition optional prompt, no count action) was signed off by the owner 2026-10-19; the test accepts either prompt shape, so W10's shape rests on that ruling, not on this test. Untested: the rule's second sentence ('it will not be possible to perform the actions for the same infinite loop again').
18-3-3.text: If an infinite loop occurs and one of the players has the ability to stop it, use the following procedure. After performing the following processing, it will not be possible to perform the actions for the same infinite loop again.

18-3-3-1.note: repeat-count declaration not modelled; per-repetition prompt satisfies 18-3-3-3 (ruling W10). The turn-player-first order of declarations is not asserted. (residual; see Resolution) W10 signed off by the owner 2026-10-19: per-repetition optional prompt, no count action, so the declaration stays unmodelled by decision. The design note in the G-ENGINE-INFINITE-LOOP-SILENTLY-CLEARED entry (2026-10-17: a count prompt per player when a signature recurs across declinable decisions) is kept only as the shape to build if W10 is reversed.
18-3-3-1.text: The turn player declares to repeat the processing a certain number of times. If the turn player doesn't have the ability to stop the infinite loop, skip this step and go on to the next step.

18-3-3-2.note: repeat-count declaration not modelled; per-repetition prompt satisfies 18-3-3-3 (ruling W10). As 18-3-3-1, for the non-turn player. (residual; see Resolution) W10 signed off 2026-10-19 (no count action): see 18-3-3-1.
18-3-3-2.text: The non-turn player declares to repeat the processing a certain number of times. If the non- turn player doesn't have the ability to stop the infinite loop, skip this step and go on to the next step.

18-3-3-3.note: Per-repetition decision (ruling W10): an optional prompt, or the DSL effect-text choose-one ('you may X instead'), lets the player repeat the loop as many times as they choose (40 / 30 in the tests, past any fixed cap), then stop it.
18-3-3-3.text: The processing is executed at least the number of times that was declared it would be repeated, then the player stops the processing when possible.

2-1.text: If the card information varies on the same cards, the card information on the newest card is always referenced.

2-10-1.text: This information indicates that a card has Overflow. (For details, refer to 4-17 "<Overflow>")

2-10-2.text: The explanation for Overflow requirements is shown using notes in card text. (For details, refer to 2-12-1-6 "Notes")

2-11-1.text: This information indicates that a card has Arts Digivolve. (For details, refer to 4-19 "Arts Digivolve")

2-11-2.text: The explanation for Arts Digivolve is shown using notes in card text. (For details, refer to 2-12-1-6 "Notes")

2-12-1.text: This is a card's sequential number. If cards have matching card names and card numbers, they're considered to be the same card.

2-13-1.text: Other information on a card can't be referenced during a game.

2-13-1-2-1.text: The name of the illustrator for the card.

2-13-1-3-1.text: The copyright notice for the card.

2-13-1-5-1.text: This icon indicates the time period when this card was released.

2-13-1-6-2.text: Notes for effects are shown in parentheses.

2-13-1-6-3.text: Sometimes a rule or effect will have notes and sometimes it won't, but they are treated the same in both situations.

2-2-1.text: This information indicates the card category for a card.

2-2-2.text: The card categories are Digi-Egg cards, Digimon cards, Tamer cards, and Option cards.

2-2-3.text: Digi-Egg cards are cards used for building Digi-Egg decks. These cards have "DIGI-EGG" written at the top edge of the card.

2-2-4.text: Digimon cards are cards used for building decks. These cards have "DIGIMON" written at the top edge of the card.

2-2-5.text: Tamer cards are cards used for building decks. These cards have "TAMER" written at the top edge of the card.

2-2-6.text: Option cards are cards used for building decks. These cards have "OPTION" written at the top edge of the card.

2-3-1-1.text: The individual card name of the card.

2-3-1-2.text: When card information is specified in an effect only using brackets, only the cards that match the name shown in brackets can be referenced. (Example: An effect that reads "[Your Turn] All of your [Marcus Damon] get +3000 DP and <Security Attack +1>" will give cards with the name [Marcus Damon] +3000 DP and <Security A. +1>.)

2-3-1-3.text: When text specifies "with [XX] in its name," cards whose names include the text in brackets can be referenced.

2-3-1-4.text: When a card has "ACE" written in its name, "ACE" is not included in the card name.

2-3-10-1.text: The requirements for Assembly. (For details, refer to 7-3 "Assembly")7-3

2-3-10-2.text: The explanation for Assembly requirements is shown using notes in card text. (For details, refer to 2-12-1-6 "Notes")

2-3-11-1.text: This refers to the text below the traits on a card. "INHERITED EFFECT", "SECURITY", "LINK", or "OPTION" will be shown for this text. Some cards don't have lower text.

2-3-11-2-1.text: An inherited effect is specific text on a card. This refers to the text marked "Inherited Effect" on a card. (For details, refer to 15-3 "Inherited Effects")

2-3-11-2-2.text: When a rule or effect references the "Inherited Effect" part of card information, the text marked "Inherited Effect" on a card is to be referenced. A card without an inherited effect section can't be referenced.

2-3-11-3-1.text: This is a [Security] effect. Some [Security] effects aren't shown in the lower text. (For details, refer to 15-16-10 "[Security]")

2-3-11-4-1.text: This information indicates that a card has [Link]. The link requirements, link DP, and link effects will be shown for a link. (For details, refer to 10 "Linking")

2-3-11-4-2.text: The link requirements show the information and the required link cost for 1 Digimon that can link with that card.

2-3-11-4-3.text: The link cost is the cost required to link that card.

2-3-11-4-4.text: The explanation for link requirements is shown using notes in card text. (For details, refer to 2-12-1-6 "Notes")

2-3-11-4-5.text: The link DP shows the DP value added to the DP of the Digimon linked to that card.

2-3-11-4-6.text: A link effect is specific text on a card. This refers to the text shown for the link effect on a card.

2-3-11-4-7.text: When a rule or effect references the "link effect" part of card information, the text for a link effect on a card is to be referenced. If a card doesn't have a link effect, it can't be referenced.

2-3-11-5-1.text: "Option information" refers to the lower text on a DUAL card.

2-3-2-1.text: This information indicates multiple traits including form, attribute, and type.

2-3-2-2.text: If a single card has multiple traits, each trait will be separated by slashes.

2-3-2-3.text: When an effect specifies "with the [XX] trait," cards with the trait that matches the text in brackets can be referenced.

2-3-2-4.text: When an effect specifies "with [XX] in any of its traits," cards with one or more traits that include4 the text in brackets can be referenced.

2-3-3-1.text: An effect is specific text on a card. This refers to the upper text on a card. (For details, refer to 15-1 "Effects")15-1

2-3-3-2.text: When a rule or effect references the "effect" part of card information, the upper text on a card is to be referenced.

2-3-3-3.text: If a rule or effect references a "persistent keyword effect" in card information, it references cards that always possess that keyword effect. (Example: An effect that specifies a card with the <Blocker> effect references cards that always possess the <Blocker> effect and does not reference cards with effects that give <Blocker> and such.)

2-3-3-4.text: If a rule or effect references a "keyword effect that executes processing" in card information, it references cards that do not involve processing conditions or optional processing conditions in the activation of that keyword effect. (Example: An effect that specifies cards with the <Blitz> effect references cards that do not involve processing conditions such as "if," "while," or "by" in the activation of that <Blitz> effect.)

2-3-4-1.text: The (Rule) icon is a rule specific to that card, not an effect. A (Rule) always applies.

2-3-4-2-1.text: A card with this (Rule) is treated as having the [XX] trait.

2-3-4-3-1.text: The name of a card with this (Rule) is also treated as [XX].

2-3-4-4-1.text: A card with this (Rule) is treated as also having [XX] in its name. However, this rule doesn't treat that card as a card with the name [XX].

2-3-4-5-1.text: The card number of a card with this (Rule) is also treated as [XX].

2-3-4-6.text: (Rule) A player can include up to X copies of cards with this card's card number in their deck.

2-3-4-6-1.text: When a card has this (Rule), up to X copies of that card can be included in a deck build.

2-3-5-1.text: This indicates information regarding the possible card for digivolution and the digivolution cost required.

2-3-5-2.text: A digivolution cost is the cost required to digivolve into that Digimon card. (For details, refer to 8-1 "Digivolving")8-1

2-3-5-3.text: Text after the [Digivolve] icon or "Digivolve:" is also included in the digivolution requirements of such cards. (Example: A card with "[Digivolve] [Koromon]: Cost 0" can digivolve from a card named [Koromon] for a cost of 0.)

2-3-6-1.text: The digivolution requirements for DNA digivolution. (For details, refer to 8-2 "DNA Digivolution")8-2

2-3-6-2.text: The explanation for DNA digivolution is shown using notes in card text. (For details, refer to 2-12- 1-6 "Notes")2-13-1-6

2-3-7-1.text: The requirements for a DigiXros. (For details, refer to 7-2 "DigiXros")7-2

2-3-7-2.text: The explanation for DigiXros requirements is shown using notes in card text. (For details, refer to 2-12- 1-6 "Notes")2-13-1-6

2-3-8-1.text: The digivolution requirements for burst digivolve. (For details, refer to 8-3 "Burst Digivolve")8-3

2-3-8-2.text: The explanation for burst digivolve is shown using notes in card text. (For details, refer to 2-12-1-6 "Notes")

2-3-9-1.text: The digivolution requirements for App Fusion. (For details, refer to 8-4 "App Fusion")8-4

2-3-9-2.text: The explanation for app fusion is shown using notes in card text. (For details, refer to 2-12-1-6 "Notes")

2-4-1.text: This information indicates the color of a card.

2-4-2.text: Colors include red, blue, yellow, green, black, purple, and white. When choosing a color by a rule or an effect, one of these colors is to be chosen.

2-4-3.text: If a single card has multiple colors, that card is a "multicolor" card.

2-4-3-1.text: A multicolor card is also treated as having all of its colors.

2-4-3-2.text: A multicolor card can't be treated as a card that doesn't have one of those colors.

2-5-1.text: This information indicates a card's strength in battles. (For details, refer to 14 "Battles")

2-5-2.text: When a rule or effect references a card's original DP, this value is to be referenced. However, if the DP was modified by an effect, the modified DP will be referenced. (For details, refer to 15-12-2 "Effects That Modify Information")

2-5-3.text: DP can't be added if a card doesn't have DP. (Example: +3000 DP can't be added if a Digimon doesn't have DP, nor can its DP be reduced by -3000.

2-6-1.text: A card's play cost refers to the cost required to play that card. This is shown using a "Play" icon.

2-7-1.text: A use cost refers to the cost required to use that card. This is shown using a "Use" icon.

2-8-1.text: This information indicates that a card is a Digi-Egg card.

2-9-1.text: This information indicates the card's level.6

2-9-2.text: Cards that have no level displayed, or with "Lv.－" shown, are treated as having no level.

3-1-1.text: Areas include the deck, Digi-Egg deck, field, hand, trash, and security stack.

3-1-2-1-1.text: All card information on cards in these areas is revealed to both players. Either player may look at the content or card order of these areas at any time.

3-1-2-2-1.text: Card information on cards in these areas isn't revealed to both players. Neither player may look at the content or card order of these areas.

3-1-3-1-1.text: When a card is moved from one area to another, that card becomes a "new card."

3-1-3-1-2.text: A new card is considered to be a different card from the card in the previous area, and it will not carry over any of the original card's statuses, states, etc.

3-1-3-1-3.text: Even if a card on the field becomes the bottom card in a stack due to cards being placed on top of it, it isn't considered to be a new card.

3-1-3-1-4.text: Even if the stacking order of stacked cards changes, they aren't considered new cards.

3-1-3-2.text: The number of cards in each area is public information.

3-1-3-3.text: When multiple cards leave an area at the same time and are then placed in a different area, they are all considered to leave and be placed at the same time rather than 1 card at a time.

3-1-3-4.text: When multiple cards leave an area at the same time, the player who owns the card that caused the action to be performed chooses the order in which the cards are placed in the new area. (Example: When "[When Digivolving] Return all of your opponent's Digimon with the highest level to the bottom of the deck in any order" is used to return multiple opponent's Digimon to the bottom of the deck at the same time, the player who activated this effect7 chooses the order in which the cards are placed at the bottom of the deck.)

3-1-3-5.text: When placing a card in an area, unless otherwise specified, it's placed according to the rules of that area. (Example: When "[On Deletion] Place this card at the bottom of your security stack" is used to place a card at the bottom of the security stack, it's placed face down.)

3-1-3-6.text: When multiple cards are moved from a public area then placed into a private area at the same time, they are placed after the order is made public.

3-1-3-7.text: If a card's information contains instructions, when placing that card in a private area, the card is placed after revealing it.

3-1-3-8.note: Authoring rule, not an engine inference: text that names no player's area is authored `to_owner: true` (the placed card's owner's stack), text that names one is authored `of: you|opponent`. `place_on_security` accepts `to_owner` with `disposition: none` (BT25-044 Junomon) and `disposition: cancel` (BT24-040 Venusmon's leave-replacement cost; owner ruling 2026-10-20, Q5781: the chosen 'other Digimon' may be either player's and goes to its owner's security). Proof limit: the security stack is the only area pinned; other unnamed-area verbs (hand/deck/trash returns) route to the owner by their own engine helpers and are not asserted here.
3-1-3-8.text: When card text specifies that a card is to be placed in an area without specifying which player's area, the card is placed in the area of the player who owns the card.

3-1-3-9.text: When Digi-Egg cards are placed from respective areas to private areas, they are placed according to the following rules.

3-1-3-9-1.text: If placing in the deck or Digi-Egg deck, cards are placed in the Digi-Egg deck in the specified order.

3-1-3-9-2.text: If placing in private areas other than the deck or Digi-Egg deck, cards are placed at the bottom of the Digi-Egg deck.

3-2-1.text: This is the area where you place your deck at the start of the game.

3-2-2.note: The deck carries its own face (every deck card is face-down); a card entering it keeps no face-down state it had as a digivolution card (3-1-3-1-2), so a later placement under a permanent that sets no face does not count it as a face-down card (4-7-9). Every deck entry goes through Player::put_on_deck_top / insert_in_deck / put_all_on_deck_top / insert_all_in_deck / put_in_deck_or_digi_egg_deck; player::tests::zone_entries_go_through_the_player_helpers keeps direct pushes (and local &mut aliases) out of src/. Proof limit: the test asserts the per-card face-down flag is cleared on entry, the engine's representation of 'the deck is face-down'; deck privacy itself (what the observation exposes) is not asserted here.
3-2-2.text: The deck is a private area. Cards are placed face-down in this area.

3-2-3.text: Players can't change the order of cards in their decks.

3-2-4.text: When multiple cards are moved from the deck to a different area at the same time, the procedure for moving them is 1 card at a time, but they are considered to be placed at the same time.

3-3-1.text: This is the area where you place your Digi-Egg deck at the start of the game.

3-3-2.note: As 3-2-2 for the Digi-Egg deck: Player::put_on_digi_egg_deck_top / insert_in_digi_egg_deck / insert_all_in_digi_egg_deck / put_in_deck_or_digi_egg_deck drop the face-down state; a Digi-Egg card returned 'to the deck' goes to the Digi-Egg deck. Proof limit as 3-2-2: the per-card flag is the representation asserted, not the area's privacy.
3-3-2.text: The Digi-egg deck is a private area. Cards are placed face- down in this area.

3-3-3.text: Players can't change the order of cards in their Digi-Egg decks.

3-3-4.text: When multiple cards are moved from the Digi-Egg deck to a different area at the same time, the procedure for moving them is 1 card at a time, but they are considered to be placed at the same time.

3-4-1.text: This is the main area of the game where cards are placed.

3-4-2.note: A card that becomes a new permanent or a new top card is face-up: Permanent::new and Permanent::push_top (digivolution, DNA, Blast DNA) clear the face-down state a digivolution card carried (3-1-3-1-2), so a card stashed face-down under a Tamer and played or digivolved into from the hand is not trashed by the rule check (17-1-3-2-4; official Q&A Q6958's mechanism, G-ENGINE-PLAY-FROM-TRASH-OF-JUST-TRASHED-SOURCE-NOT-PLAYED).
3-4-2.text: The field is a public area. Cards are placed face-up in this area.

3-4-3.text: When cards are placed in the field, they are placed unsuspended. (For details, refer to 4-11 "Card Orientation")

3-4-4.text: Each card placed on the field is treated as a separate Digimon or Tamer, etc.

3-4-5.text: If another card is stacked on top of a card on the field, or if the card stacked on top leaves and the card underneath is a different card, it will be considered to have changed to that Digimon or Tamer, etc. It won't be considered a different Digimon or Tamer, etc. (Example: If a player's [GrapLeomon] digivolves into [Marsmon], that [GrapLeomon] will be considered to change into [Marsmon], it won't be treated as a [Marsmon] that is newly placed onto the field.)

3-4-6.text: The field is divided into the breeding area and the battle area.

3-4-7-1.text: This is the part of the field where hatched Digimon are placed.

3-4-7-2.text: Only 1 card can be placed in the breeding area.

3-4-7-3.text: Cards in breeding areas can't be affected by effects, except for effects that explicitly specify or reference breeding areas. (For details, refer to 15-15-6 "Isn't affected by effects" cards")15-15-5

3-4-7-4.text: Effects on cards in breeding areas can't trigger or activate, except for effects that explicitly specify or reference breeding areas. (Example: Even when a Digimon with a [When Digivolving] effect in a breeding area digivolves, its [When Digivolving] effect doesn't trigger.)8

3-4-7-5.text: Cards in breeding areas can't be chosen for effects, except for effects that explicitly specify or reference breeding areas. (Example: A Digimon in your opponent's breeding area can't be chosen for "[On Play] Suspend 1 of your opponent's Digimon."

3-4-7-6.note: A breeding-area digivolution cannot meet <Digisorption>'s trigger condition (the rule's own example is a breeding digivolution not triggering 'when your Digimon digivolves'); DCGO BT2_047.cs gates on a battle-area permanent. Pinned with Task 16 (Plan 4).
3-4-7-6.text: Trigger conditions can't be met by cards in breeding areas, except for effects that explicitly specify or reference breeding areas. (Example: Even if your Digimon in the breeding area digivolves during your turn, a "[Your Turn] When your Digimon digivolves, by suspending this Tamer, <Draw 1>" effect doesn't trigger.)

3-4-7-7.text: Activation conditions can't be met by cards in breeding areas, except for effects that explicitly specify or reference breeding areas. (Example: Even if your opponent has a Digimon in the breeding area at the start of your main phase, a "[Start of Your Main Phase] If your opponent has a Digimon, gain 1 memory" effect doesn't trigger.)

3-4-7-8.text: Information on cards in breeding areas can't be referenced, except for effects that explicitly specify or reference breeding areas. (Example: Even if you have a Digimon with the [Armor Form] trait in the breeding area, you can't ignore the color requirements when a "while you have a Digimon with the [Armor Form] trait, you may ignore this card's color requirements" effect activates.

3-4-8-1.text: This is the part of the field where cards are placed.

3-4-8-2.text: Any number of cards can be placed in the battle area.

3-5-1.text: This is the area where cards held by each player are placed.

3-5-2.text: Players can change the order of cards in their respective hand at any time.

3-5-3.note: A hand card carries no face-down placement: every hand entry goes through Player::put_in_hand / insert_in_hand / put_all_in_hand, which clear the face-down state (3-1-3-1-2); player::tests::zone_entries_go_through_the_player_helpers keeps direct pushes out of src/.
3-5-3.text: The hand is a private area, but the cards' owner may always look at their hand.

3-6-1.text: The trash is the area where trashed cards are placed.

3-6-2.text: Players can change the order of cards in their respective trash at any time.

3-6-3.note: Every trash entry goes through Player::put_in_trash / insert_in_trash / put_all_in_trash (face-up); player::tests::zone_entries_go_through_the_player_helpers keeps direct pushes out of src/.
3-6-3.text: The trash is a public area. Cards are placed face-up in a stack in this area.

3-7-1.text: Security cards are placed in this area.

3-7-2.note: A card placed in the security stack with no face specified is face-down (also 3-1-3-5's example): the engine records the face by Player::face_up_security membership (absent = face-down), and the security-entry helpers (Player::put_on_security_top / insert_in_security) clear the per-card face-down state a digivolution card carried (3-1-3-1-2) instead of duplicating the face; an opaque-deck placeholder keeps its marker. The arriving card is a new card placed face down: insert_in_security also removes a stale face_up_security record for it (pre-existing, fixed under Task 38); a face-up placement (3-7-4) marks it after the insert.
3-7-2.text: The security stack is a private area. Cards in this area are placed face-down and spread out so that the number of cards can be seen.

3-7-3.text: Players can't change the order of cards in their security stacks.

3-7-4.text: If a face-up card is placed in a security stack, the card becomes public information.

3-7-5.text: When multiple cards are moved from the security stack to a different area at the same time, the procedure for moving them is 1 card at a time, but they are considered to be placed at the same time.

4-1-1.text: Memory refers to the resource used to pay for in-game costs.

4-1-2.text: "X or less memory" refers to X on your side of the memory gauge or further to the right. "X or more memory" refers to X on your side of the memory gauge or further to the left. (Example: "[Start of Your Turn] If you have 2 or less memory, set it to 3" includes a condition where the memory must be at 2 on your side or further to the right.)

4-1-3.text: "If your opponent has X or less memory" refers to X on your opponent's side of the memory gauge or further to the left. "If your opponent has X or more memory" refers to X on your opponent's side of the memory gauge or further to the right. (Example: A "[When Digivolving] <Blitz> (This Digimon can attack when your opponent has 1 or more memory)" effect includes a condition where the memory must be at 1 on your opponent's side or further to the right.)

4-1-4.text: "Gain X memory" means moving the memory marker X spaces toward your side (the left side) of the memory gauge. "Lose X memory" means moving the memory marker X spaces toward your opponent's side (the right side) of the memory gauge.

4-10-1.text: A linked card is a card that has a link card.

4-11-1.text: A "player" refers to a game participant.

4-11-2.text: If a rule or effect specifies an "owner," it refers to the player that is currently using that card in the game.

4-11-3.text: "Opponent" refers to the other player in the game.

4-12-1.text: The turn player refers to the player that is performing the procedures for the current turn, and the non-turn player refers to the other player.

4-13-1.text: Cards on the field have an orientation. A card's orientation shows whether it is unsuspended or suspended.

4-13-1-1-1.text: An "unsuspended" card refers to a card placed vertically.11

4-13-1-1-2.text: "Unsuspended state" refers to an unsuspended card.

4-13-1-2-1.text: A "suspended" card refers to a card placed horizontally.

4-13-1-2-2.text: "Suspended state" refers to a suspended card.

4-14-1.text: "Drawing" refers to drawing cards from the deck and placing them in the hand.

4-14-2.text: Unless specified otherwise by a rule or effect, a player draws cards from their own deck.

4-15-1.text: When deletion processing is applied to a card by a rule or effect, that card is trashed.

4-15-2.text: An effect timing or keyword effect that triggers on deletion of the card itself does so in the area where the card is deleted, then becomes pending activation after that card is placed into the trash by destruction. (Example: An [On Deletion] effect triggers in the battle area, then becomes pending activation after the card is placed into the trash.)

4-16-1.text: "Trashing" refers to placing a card in the trash.

4-16-2.text: An effect that triggers on trashing of the card itself does so in the area where the card is trashed, then becomes pending activation after that card is placed into the trash by trashing. (Example: "When this card is trashed from your hand by one of your effects, <Draw 1>" will trigger while the card is in the hand, then it will become pending activation when the card is in the trash.)

4-17-1.text: "Moving" refers to moving a Digimon between the breeding area and the battle area. A player can move a Digimon from the breeding area to the battle area as one of their actions during the breeding phase.

4-17-2.text: Only Digimon with DP can be moved.

4-17-3.text: When a card is moved, it keeps its orientation. (For details, refer to 4-11 "Card Orientation")4-13

4-17-4.text: Any effects applied to a Digimon before it moves are kept after the move.

4-17-5.text: If a Digimon is moved, the effects status of that Digimon isn't carried over. (Example: If a Digimon has an effect that's pending activation when it's moved, that effect will no longer be pending activation.) (For details, refer to 15-4 "Effect States") 15-4

4-18-1.text: "Hatching" refers to flipping over the top card of your Digi-Egg deck and placing it in the specified area. You can hatch a Digi-Egg from the top of your Digi-Egg deck into the breeding area as one of your actions during the breeding phase.

4-18-2.text: You can't hatch a Digi-Egg if you don't have any cards in your Digi-Egg deck.

4-18-3.text: You can't hatch a Digi-Egg if you already have a card in the breeding area.

4-19-1.note: <Overflow <-3>> owner loses 3 when the ACE is deleted from the field, returned to the hand, or trashed from under a card; control: a non-ACE moves nothing. Proven via the `ace_overflow` card field; no matrix row.
4-19-1.text: <Overflow> is a rule on Digimon ACE cards. When a card with <Overflow> moves from the field or from under a card to another area, the memory marker is moved according to the value specified for <Overflow>.

4-19-2.note: 'Delete 1 of your Digimon. Then, gain 1 memory.' on own ACE: -3 (no source) precedes the +1.
4-19-2.text: When <Overflow> causes the memory marker to move, the processing for moving it is performed immediately, even if the processing for another action is already being performed.

4-19-3.note: Playing or digivolving into the ACE moves only the paid cost.
4-19-3.text: <Overflow> isn't processed when a card is moved from another area to the field. (For details, refer to 3-4 "The Field")3-4

4-19-4.note: An ACE placed from the hand as a bottom digivolution card moves no memory.
4-19-4.text: <Overflow> isn't processed when a card is moved from another area to under a card. (For details, refer to 4-5 "Stacked Cards")4-7

4-19-5.note: A deletion batch (mutual battle deletion, 'delete all Digimon') collects every leaving card and processes its <Overflow> instances in one pass after the removals, before the batch's trigger flush. A rule check that both trashes and deletes ACE stacks (§17-1-3) applies the trashed cards' turn-player instances before the deletion batch and the non-turn player's after it, so every turn-player instance goes first (engine test ace_overflow::rule_check_deleted_and_trashed_aces_overflow_turn_player_first; not listed in tests because it lives outside rules_conformance and carries no cite!).
4-19-5.text: When multiple instances of <Overflow> are processed simultaneously, they are processed using the following procedure.

4-19-5-1.note: The turn player's instances go first: mutual battle deletion of two ACEs at memory 9 gives 9 -> 6 -> 9; 'delete all Digimon' (two P0 ACEs, one P1 ACE) gives 9 -> 6 -> 3 -> 6. The turn player's choice among their own instances is unobservable (same direction), so no prompt.
4-19-5-1.text: The turn player chooses 1 instance of <Overflow> on their cards and processes it. The turn player repeats this procedure until there are no more unresolved instances of <Overflow> on their cards.

4-19-5-2.note: The non-turn player's instances are processed after all of the turn player's (one apply_ace_overflow_for_sources pass per deletion batch).
4-19-5-2.text: Once all instances of <Overflow> on the turn player's cards have been processed, then the non- turn player chooses 1 instance of <Overflow> on12 their cards and processes it. The non-turn player repeats this procedure until there are no more unresolved instances of <Overflow> on their cards.

4-2-1.text: A cost is a numerical value that is required to be paid using memory. A card's cost and "pay X cost" are both examples of costs.

4-2-2.text: To pay a cost, the player moves the memory gauge toward the opponent's side (to their right) by an amount equal to the numerical value of the cost. When paying, the value indicated is paid, and no more and no less than that value can be paid.

4-2-3-1.text: If a cost's numerical value increases or decreases, that becomes an alternate cost. When a cost becomes an alternate cost, no more and no less than that value can be paid. (Example: If a card with a play cost of 12 activates the effect "When this card would be played, if you have an [Iliad] trait Tamer, reduce the cost by 5," the cost to be paid becomes an alternate cost of 7.)

4-20-1.note: After the used DUAL's [Main], P0 may digivolve a Lv.5 into it instead of trashing: no digivolution cost paid; declining trashes it.
4-20-1.text: Arts Digivolve is a rule on DUAL cards. Instead of the trashing from the pending processing after using an Option card, one of your cards on the field may digivolve into that DUAL card without paying the cost.

4-20-2.note: Overwrite: the card is not in the trash at the decision and never reaches it when accepted. Matrix row ArtsDigivolve (optional) agrees.
4-20-2.text: Arts Digivolve is overwrite processing that replaces the trashing of an Option card from the pending processing. (For details, refer to 18-1 "Pending Processing")

4-21-1.text: Tokens are non-game cards played by effects. Such effects play tokens as if they have card information.

4-21-2.text: The number of tokens is always public information.

4-21-3.text: Cards can't be stacked with tokens.
