4-21-5.text: When a token leaves the field, it is removed from the game instead of being placed in another area. However, the token itself is considered to be placed in that area.

4-22-1.text: "Color requirements" refers to a requirement that must be met in order to use an Option card. (For details, refer to 9 "Using Cards")9

4-22-2.text: To meet color requirements, you must have a Digimon or Tamer on your field that's the same color as the Option card you want to use.

4-22-3.text: An Option card with multiple colors can't be used unless the color requirements are met for all of its colors.

4-22-4.text: A multicolor Digimon or multicolor Tamer can meet the color requirements for multiple colors.

4-22-5.text: An Option card's color requirements don't have to be met when activating its effects without using it.

4-23-1.text: A "with XX in its text" card is a card that has the "XX" term or icon in the information printed on that card. (Example: A "card with <Save> in its text" refers to a card with the <Save> icon included in the information on that card.) (For details, refer to 2-3 "Information Written on Cards")

4-23-2.text: When an effect is gained, that doesn't mean that text is gained. (Example: A Digimon won't gain the <Save> text from a digivolution card whose inherited effect reads "[Your Turn] While this Digimon has <Save> in its text, it gets +2000 DP.")

4-23-3.text: When a card with an effect's text is specified, as long as the card has that text written on it, it can be referenced even in situations where the effect can't be triggered or activated. (Example: A card with <Save> shown in its inherited effect is considered a card with <Save> in its text even when that card isn't placed in digivolution cards.)

4-23-4.text: When a card with an icon's text is specified, only a card with the matching icon can be referenced. (Example: When an effect specifies a card with <Save> in its text, <Material Save> can't be referenced because its icon isn't the same.)

4-23-5.text: Notes aren't included in text. (Example: A Digimon card with <Alliance> and <Security A.> in the notes enclosed in parentheses for Alliance isn't considered to have <Security A.> in its text.)

4-24-1.text: When a card shows "XX/YY," it means the same as "XX or YY," and either one of them will meet a requirement. However, this doesn't include when individual traits are separated by slashes. (Example: "[On Play] 1 of your opponent's Digimon/Tamers can't suspend until the end of their turn" means that you choose 1 of your opponent's Digimon or Tamers, then the chosen card can't suspend.)

4-25-1.text: A "with different XX" card refers to a card whose information is different from the information specified using XX.

4-25-2.text: If a card that has multiple instances of the information specified by XX, the differing portions can be referenced and be treated as differing combinations.

4-26-1.text: "With/have X cards" refers to a requirement that is fulfilled when that number of cards is present. (Example: "[On Play] When this Digimon has 3 digivolution cards,13 <Blitz>" can be activated if that Digimon has 3 or more digivolution cards.)

4-27-1.text: "Each" or "every" is used when an effect references a number of something.

4-27-2.text: Processing that targets "for each X" number of stacked cards from the top or bottom targets up to that number of cards in order starting from that position in the stack. (Example: If an effect reads "[On Play] [When Digivolving] For each of your Digimon with the [Royal Knight] trait or each of your blue Tamers, trash the top 2 digivolution cards of 1 of your opponent's Digimon" and you have 2 blue Tamers, you would choose 1 of your opponent's Digimon and trash its top 4 digivolution cards.)

4-27-3.text: In the case of a "process A and process B" effect that applies to each X, after processing A for each X present upon activation, you then process B for each X present upon activation. (Example: For text that reads "[End of Opponent’s Turn] [Once Per Turn] For each of this Digimon's link cards, trash your opponent's top security card and return 1 of their Digimon to the bottom of the deck," if that Digimon is linked to 3 cards, you trash your opponent's top 3 security cards and then return 3 of their Digimon to the bottom of the deck.

4-27-4.text: A triggering from 1 trigger condition is considered to only trigger once, even if it occurred multiple times at the same time, but if the effect text contains "each" or "every," the specified number can be referenced. (Example: If an effect reads "[All Turns] When an opponent's Digimon is deleted, gain 1 memory for each Digimon deleted" and multiple opponent Digimon are deleted at the same time, 1 memory is gained for each Digimon deleted.)

4-28-1.text: An "Option card in the battle area" refers to an Option card that was placed in the battle area by an effect. (Example: A "trash an Option card in the battle area" effect can only trash an Option card that was placed in the battle area by an effect.)

4-29-1.text: "Also" indicates that effects given by that processing share the same duration and targets as the processing that proceeded them. (Example: "They also" in the effect "{Security} [Your Turn] All of your red or blue [TS] trait Digimon gain <Alliance>. While you have [Apollomon] or [Dianamon], they also gain <Rush>" refers to your red or blue [TS] trait Digimon.)

4-3-1.text: Digi-Egg cards and Digimon cards placed on the field are treated as Digimon.

4-3-2.text: Cards stacked under Digimon are considered "digivolution cards," regardless of their card category. (For details, refer to 4-6 "Digivolution Cards")

4-3-3.text: A Digimon gains the inherited effects of the digivolution cards placed under it. (Example: If a Digimon has a digivolution card that has <Piercing> in its inherited effects, that Digimon will have <Piercing>.)

4-3-4.text: A Digimon gets the link DP value on its link card.

4-3-5.text: A Digimon gains the link effects on its link card.

4-3-6.text: Digimon in the battle area can attack. (For details, refer to 11 "Attacking")11

4-3-7.text: Digimon with <Blocker> in the battle area can block. (For details, refer to 12 "Blocking")12

4-3-8.text: Digimon can perform 1 security check. (For details, refer to 13 "Security Checks")13

4-4-1.text: Tamer cards placed on the field are treated as Tamers.

4-4-2.text: When placing a card under a Tamer that already has cards stacked under it, unless specified otherwise, you place the new card at the bottom. (Example: If using <Save> to place a card under a Tamer that already has cards stacked under it, place the new card at the bottom.)

4-5-1.text: A Digimon card flipped over from the security stack upon a security check is treated as a Security Digimon. (For details, refer to 13 "Security Checks")

4-6-1.note: In the hand a DUAL is offered both as an Option (use) and as a Digimon (digivolve), and matches both 'Digimon card' and 'Option card' trait searches; an unqualified reference (no category named) reads the Digimon information only (owner ruling W5 (b), 2026-10-17; Task 29 superseded the provisional reading (a)): 'red card' finds the red-Digimon / purple-Option DUAL, 'purple card', 'blue card', 'purple Lv.6 card' and 'card that is not red' do not (test renamed from dual_unqualified_colour_reference_matches_either_information).
4-6-1.text: A DUAL card is a card that can be treated as being in either the Digimon card category or the Option card category.

4-6-2.note: The two declarations are distinct actions in the mask (use bit vs digivolve bit).
4-6-2.text: When using a DUAL card, the player must declare whether they are digivolving with the Digimon information or using the Option information on that card.

4-6-3.note: The rule's example: 'trash 1 of your opponent's Option cards in the battle area' never takes the DUAL stack (trashes a real field Option instead, or nothing); 'delete 1 Digimon' deletes it. Zone split (Task 37, official Q&A Q6395 / Q6404): the rule governs the DUAL card AS the permanent -- the TOP card of a battle-area or breeding stack (Game::card_is_permanent_top_card) is a Digimon whatever the reference. A DUAL card lying in a permanent's digivolution or link cards is read by what the reference names: an unqualified reference reads the Digimon information (red found, purple not; W5 (b)), a 'Digimon card' reference finds it, and an 'Option card' reference finds it too and reads its Option information (4-6-6-2). Task 18's reading that every DUAL card on the field, digivolution cards included, can't be referenced as an Option card was contradicted by Q6395 and re-pinned (the 'Option card' self-source count now counts it; test renamed from dual_digivolution_card_counts_as_digimon_only).
4-6-3.text: A DUAL card placed on the field is treated as a Digimon. It can't be referenced as an Option card placed on the field. (Example: A DUAL card that is digivolved by placing it on top of one of your cards on the field will be treated as a Digimon, and it can't be trashed by a "trash an Option card in the battle area" effect.)

4-6-4.note: One card carries both: digivolving reads the Digimon information (cost 3, 12000 DP), using reads the Option information (cost 2, purple).
4-6-4.text: A single DUAL card has both Digimon information and Option information.

4-6-5-1.note: The trait is matched when the hand card is referenced as a Digimon card. Proof limit: no negative control (a non-[Artsy] DUAL card not picked) in this test.
4-6-5-1.text: This refers to a DUAL card's traits and the information above them.

4-6-5-2.note: Digivolution cost/level/DP from the Digimon information; a 'level 6 Digimon card' hand search matches it.
4-6-5-2.text: A DUAL card's Digimon information can be referenced when referencing the card as a Digimon card or Digimon.

4-6-5-3.note: The Digimon information's [When Digivolving] is a Digimon effect: blocked by 'not affected by your opponent's Digimon effects', like a plain Digimon's (control).
4-6-5-3.text: Effects in the Digimon information are considered Digimon effects. (For details, refer to 15-2 "Effect Types")

4-6-6-1.note: The trait is matched when the hand card is referenced as an Option card.
4-6-6-1.text: This refers a DUAL card's traits and the information below them.

4-6-6-2.note: Option USE reads the Option information (purple color requirement, use cost 2). Card-zone searches now reference the Option information when the search is for an Option card: 'purple Option card' finds the DUAL, 'red Option card' and 'purple Digimon card' don't (both directions pinned, so a both-faces-union fix fails). Also for a DUAL card lying in a Digimon's digivolution cards (official Q&A Q6395, LadyDevimon BT25-083 / BeelStarmon BT25-085): 'By trashing 1 Option card from any of your Digimon's digivolution cards, you may use 1 [Artsy] trait Option card from your trash with the cost reduced by 1' finds the DUAL card, trashes it, and uses that same card from the trash (use cost 2 - 1 paid, its [Main] resolves); an 'Option card' self-source count counts it; and it reads the Option INFORMATION there too: 'purple Option card from the digivolution cards' finds the red-Digimon / purple-Option DUAL, 'red Option card' and 'purple Digimon card' don't (the digivolution-zone twin of the hand pins). The hard-coded stack Option searches (trash_option_from_own_stacks, EX7-048's digivolution-card Option trash) and the 15-7-4 union-zone payability guard read it the same way.
4-6-6-2.text: A DUAL card's Option information can be referenced when referencing the card as an Option card.

4-6-6-3.note: The Option information's [Main] is an Option card effect: blocked by 'not affected by your opponent's Option cards' effects', like a plain Option's (control).
4-6-6-3.text: Effects in the Option information are treated as Option card effects. (For details, refer to 15-2 "Effect Types")

4-7-1.text: "Stacked cards" refers to all of the 1 or more cards in a10 stack of cards on the field.

4-7-10.text: A face-down card under another card is hidden information, but the cards' owner may freely look at the content of a face-down card under one of their cards.

4-7-3.text: The stacking order of cards can't be changed.

4-7-4.text: The bottom cards of a stack are spread out so that inherited effects are visible. A card without an inherited effect is placed in the stack so that its name is visible. A face-down card must be stacked so that it's clearly under the top card.

4-7-5.text: Unless specified otherwise, the bottom cards of a stack are placed face-up.

4-7-6.text: Bottom cards of a stack are placed vertically, but they don't have an orientation. When the bottom card of a stack becomes the top card, the stack's previous orientation is carried over. This isn't considered unsuspending or suspending of a card. (Example: When <De-Digivolve 1> is used to trash the top card of a suspended Digimon, the top card of the stack under it will carry over the suspended state.)

4-7-7.note: Controller ruling, OWNER-DECIDED 2026-10-19 (the project's reading): the bottom cards are part of the top card's information -- they contribute inherited effects (4-7-4) -- but a Digimon's traits are its top card's (with its (Rule) Trait grants, 2-3-4-2); a [TS] digivolution card does not make the Digimon a [TS] Digimon. The manual has no explicit 'traits are the top card's' sentence; official Q&A Q3225 (EX1-038: trashing the top card leaves a Digimon 'without [Free] in its traits' while the [Free] EX1-038 is still a digivolution card) and DCGO (BT25_020.cs / EX8_047.cs read permanent.TopCard) are the ruling. Counted: the battle-winner trait qualifier ('any of your [TS] trait Digimon win a battle') and the host-Digimon trait predicate ('trash this card from a [TS] trait Digimon's digivolution cards') read the top card, each with a top-card control (G-ENGINE-BATTLE-WINNER-TRAIT-READS-DIGIVOLUTION-CARDS resolved). Status (review round 1): the tests pin the Q3225 / DCGO top-card reading of the characteristics consequence; neither sentence is proven as written; the second sentence (bottom cards not on the field; place-under removes) is untested. EX1-038's own inherited text ('[Imperialdramon] in its name or [Free] in its traits', while EX1-038 itself is [Free]) is the strongest card-text evidence for the top-card reading. Name: Controller ruling (Tasks 31 / 35; owner-decided 2026-10-19): 4-7-7 governs stack membership; a Digimon's characteristics (name, traits) are its top card's -- official Q&A Q3225 (EX1-038: after its top card is trashed the Digimon is 'without [Free] in its traits or [Imperialdramon] in its name' although EX1-038 [Free] stays in the stack; EX1-038's own 'While this Digimon has [Imperialdramon] in its name or [Free] in its traits' would always hold under a stack scan) and DCGO TopCard reads. digimon_name_is_the_top_cards_name pins the NAME half ('While this Digimon has [Greymon] in its name': a [Greymon] digivolution card under a non-[Greymon] top card gives no +1000; G-DSL-CARRIER-NAME-READS-DIGIVOLUTION-CARDS). Neither sentence is proven as written; the second sentence (not on the field / place-under removes from the field) is untested. Status stays `gap` on purpose: the tests prove the signed-off characteristics reading, not this rule unit's own two sentences -- a cheap follow-up test (bottom cards contribute inherited effects per 4-7-4; placing a card under a Tamer removes it from the field) would flip it.
4-7-7.text: The bottom cards of a stack are treated as part of the information on the top card. They aren't considered to be placed on the field. (Example: When "[When Digivolving] Place one of your opponent's level 3 or lower Digimon under another of your opponent's Digimon as its bottom digivolution card or under an opponent's Tamer" is used to place a Digimon under a card, that card is considered to be removed from the field.)

4-7-8.text: When a card with cards stacked under it would be removed from the field, the cards under it are trashed at the same time. (Example: When a Digimon or Tamer would be removed from the battle area, any cards under it are trashed at the same time.)

4-7-9.text: A face-down card under another card is considered to be a card without card information, and its information can't be referenced. (Example: When a face-down digivolution card is placed for <Training>, information such as its card name or color can't be referenced for other effects.)

4-8-1.note: A digivolution card is a card UNDER a Digimon: an effect that trashes a Digimon's top card ('trash the top card of 1 of your Digimon', the Burst Digivolve turn-end idiom; 'trash the top 2 stacked cards', BT21-030) trashes no digivolution card -- the source-trash observer does not trigger and the top-card-trashed observer triggers once per event (once for a 2-card batch); <De-Digivolve> is the same case (16-12-1, ch16_processing_keywords::de_digivolve_trashes_top_cards_not_digivolution_cards). G-ENGINE-TRASH-TOP-SOURCE-FIRES-DIGIVOLUTION-CARD-TRASHED resolved 2026-10-17.
4-8-1.text: A digivolution card refers to a card placed under a Digimon. (For details, refer to 4-5 "Stacked Cards")4-7

4-8-2.note: Proven for names: 'While [Greymon] is in this Digimon's digivolution cards' (production idiom self_digivolution_sources_contain_name, BT16-027 / BT20-020 / BT20-102) is not satisfied by a [Greymon] top card and is satisfied by a [Greymon] digivolution card. The same test pins the converse for 4-7-7 (a Digimon's name is its top card's). Traits / level / colour of digivolution cards are not staged here.
4-8-2.text: When referencing digivolution card information, the information is referenced on cards that are treated as digivolution cards.

4-9-1.text: A link card is a card plugged in sideways upon a link.

4-9-2.text: A link card isn't considered a stacked card. (For details, refer to 4-5 "Stacked Cards")4-7

4-9-3.text: A link card is plugged in from the right and positioned so that the link portion of the card is visible. When multiple link cards are inserted under 1 card, a newly inserted link card must be placed so that its link portion is visible under the existing cards.

4-9-4.text: A link card isn't considered to be a card on the field. (For details, refer to 3-4 "The Field")3-4

4-9-5.note: Base limit 1 (Game::link_limit). Every link at the limit replaces existing link cards in the link itself: a declared link (link_max_base_is_one, declared_link_at_limit_replaces_existing_link_card_by_choice), an effect's link_cards pick (effect_link_at_limit_replaces_existing_link_card_by_choice) and an effect relinking its own Digimon (effect_relink_at_limit_offers_the_same_choice). With 2+ existing link cards and fewer to replace, the linking player chooses which (one shared LinkCardTrashChoice frame; §10-1-3-1, W12); the new card is never an option and no later 17-1-3-2-5 trim follows. With nothing to choose the replaced cards are trashed directly. The rule-check trims excess_link_cards_* are ch17's 17-1-3-2-5.
4-9-5.text: 1 card can have a maximum of 1 link card. When linking to a Digimon that has already reached the link limit, the same number of the existing link cards are trashed at the same time as the newly linked cards.

4-9-6.text: If a card with a link card would become a new card, its link card is trashed at the same time. (For details, refer to 3- 1-3-1 "New Cards")3-1-3-1

5-1-1.text: Before beginning a game, both players prepare the items required for a game. (For details, refer to 1-4 "Items Required for a Game")1-4

5-1-2.text: Token cards are left outside of the game at this point.

5-1-3.text: Place the Index (Quick Reference Guide for Keyword Effects and Rules) to the side of your play sheet or away from your other cards. (For details, refer to 1-4-5 "Index (Quick Reference Guide for Keyword Effects and Rules)")

5-2-1.text: Before the game begins, both players must perform the following steps.

5-2-1-1.text: Each player shuffles their respective deck. Then, both players place their deck face down.

5-2-1-2.text: Each player shuffles their respective Digi-Egg deck. Then, both players place their Digi-Egg deck face down. If you don't have a Digi-Egg deck, proceed directly to the next step.

5-2-1-3.text: The players use rock-paper-scissors to determine the first player and the second player. The player who wins the game of rock-paper-scissors goes first.

5-2-1-4.text: Both players draw 5 cards from their decks for their initial hands. Then, both players starting with the first player may declare to re-draw their initial hand, but this can only be done once by each player.

5-2-1-5.text: After declaring a re-draw, the player returns their entire hand to their deck, shuffles it, then draws 5 cards for their new initial hand.

5-2-1-6.text: For their security stack, both players take the top 5 cards of their deck and place them face-down one at a time without looking at the fronts of the cards.14 The cards are to be placed so the top card of the deck becomes the bottom card of the security stack.

5-2-1-7.text: Place the memory gauge marker at the 0 position.

5-2-1-8.text: The game begins with the first player's turn.

6-1-1.text: A game will proceed with one of the players as the turn player.

6-1-2.text: A turn proceeds using phases in the following order. Unsuspend phase, draw phase, breeding phase, and main phase.

6-1-3.text: The next phase won't begin until all of the processing is resolved for the current phase.

6-1-4-1.text: The turn end conditions are met when the memory is at 1 or more on your opponent's side and all processing has been resolved for the current phase. Then, the turn will end with the current phase. (For details, refer to 6-6 "End of Turn")6-6

6-2-1.text: The turn starts with the turn player unsuspending all of their cards on the field at the same time.

6-2-1-1.text: If there are any rules or effects to be processed when the turn starts, the processing takes place before the unsuspending processing for the unsuspend phase. (Example: "[Start of Your Turn] If you have 2 or less memory, set it to 3" is processed before the unsuspending processing for the unsuspend phase.)

6-2-1-2.text: If processing for any rules or effects has been resolved when the turn starts and the turn end conditions have been met, the end of the turn timing occurs before unsuspending.

6-2-1-3.text: Cards don't have to be unsuspended in any particular order for the unsuspend phase.

6-3-1-1.text: The first player doesn't draw a card during the draw phase of their first turn. A card must be drawn in all subsequent draw phases.

6-4-1.text: 1 of the following actions can be performed by the turn player during the breeding phase. Hatch a Digi-Egg, move a card from the breeding area to the battle area, or do nothing.

6-4-1-1.text: "Hatch a Digi-Egg" means taking the top card of your Digi-Egg deck and placing it face-up in the breeding area. (For details, refer to 4-16 "Hatching a Digi-Egg")4-18

6-4-1-2.text: "Move a card from the breeding area to the battle area" means moving your Digimon from the breeding area to the battle area. (For details, refer to 4-15 "Moving Cards")4-17

6-4-1-3.text: "Do nothing" means proceeding to the next phase without doing anything.

6-5-1.text: During the main phase, the turn player can perform the following actions in any order any number of times. These actions are to be performed when there is no unresolved processing. Play a Digimon card or Tamer card from the hand, digivolve into a Digimon card from the hand, use an Option card from the hand, link a card from the hand or battle area, attack, activate an activation-type effect, or pass.

6-5-1-1.text: Play a Digmon Card or Tamer Card From the Hand

6-5-1-1-1.text: This action is where the cost is paid for a Digimon card or Tamer card in the hand in order to play it into the battle area. (For details, refer to 7-1 "Playing a Card")7-1

6-5-1-1-2.text: When performing this action, it is also possible to DigiXros the played Digimon card. (For details, refer to 7-2 "DigiXros")7-2

6-5-1-1-3.text: When performing this action, it is also possible to use [Assembly] on the played Digimon card. (For details, refer to 7-3 "Assembly")7-3

6-5-1-2.text: Digivolve Into a Digimon Card From the Hand

6-5-1-2-1.text: Digivolving a Digimon is an action where a player's card on the field is digivolved into 1 Digimon card in the hand by paying its cost. (For details, refer to 8-115 "Digivolving")8-1

6-5-1-2-2.text: This action can also be used to digivolve multiple Digimon in your battle area into 1 Digimon card with [DNA Digivolution] in the hand by paying its cost. (For details, refer to 8-2 "DNA Digivolution")8-2

6-5-1-2-3.text: This action can also be used to digivolve one of your cards on the field into 1 Digimon card with [Burst Digivolve] by paying its cost. (For details, refer to 8-3 "Burst Digivolve")

6-5-1-2-4.text: This action can also be used to digivolve 1 of a player's Digimon in the battle area into 1 Digimon card with [App Fusion] in the hand by paying its cost. (For details, refer to 8-4 "App Fusion")

6-5-1-3.text: Use an Option Card From the Hand

6-5-1-3-1.text: This action is where a player pays the cost for an Option card in the hand to use it from their hand. (For details, refer to 9-1 "Using Cards")9-1

6-5-1-4.text: Linking a Card in the Hand or Battle Area

6-5-1-4-1.text: This action is where 1 card from the hand or battle area is linked with 1 of your Digimon in the battle area. (For details, refer to 10 "Linking")10

6-5-1-5-1.text: This action is where a player uses their Digimon in the battle area to attack. (For details, refer to 11 "Attacking")11

6-5-1-6-1.text: This action is where a player activates 1 activation-type effect on one of their cards.

6-5-1-7-1.text: This action is where a player declares a pass. After declaring a pass, the memory is immediately moved to 3 on the opponent's side.

6-6-1.text: When the turn end conditions are met, the turn will end with the current phase. (For details, refer to 6-1-4 "Turn End Conditions")6-1-4

6-6-2.text: Even if the timing for the end of the turn arrives, the current phase will continue until all processing has been resolved.

6-6-3.text: Once all processing has been resolved for the end of the turn timing, the end of the turn will arrive, then the non- turn player's turn will begin.

6-6-4.note: After a pass, [End of Your Turn] effects bring the memory back to 2 on the turn player's side: the turn player and the main phase continue.
6-6-4.text: If the memory moves to 0 or more at the end of the turn, the end of the turn will be postponed and the current phase will continue.

7-1-1.text: "Playing a card" refers to a rule where a player can place a new card with a play cost onto the field. A card can be played from a player's hand into the battle area as part of their main phase actions. (For details, refer to 6-5 "Main Phase")6-5

7-1-2-1.text: A Digimon or Tamer, etc. can't attack on the turn it was placed on the field.

7-1-2-2.text: Immediate-type effects that trigger when a card would be played will trigger immediately after the card is revealed during the play procedure. (For details, refer to 15-8-5 "Immediate-Type Effects")15-8-5

7-1-2-3.text: If a card can no longer be played after revealing it as part of the procedure for playing it, the revealed card is returned to its original location. This isn't considered removal from an area. In addition, the memory doesn't move when a card can't be played because its cost can't be paid.

7-1-3.text: The processing for playing a card is performed using the following procedure.

7-1-3-1.text: The player declares to play a card and reveals that card.

7-1-3-2.text: The player pays the specified play cost. (For details, refer to 2-6 "Play Costs")2-6

7-1-3-3.text: The card is placed on the field and the card playing procedure is resolved.

7-2-1.text: A DigiXros refers to a rule where a player plays a Digimon card with DigiXros requirements, places any number of the cards specified in that card's DigiXros requirements from their hand and/or battle area under the Digimon card to be played, and the play cost is reduced by the value specified in the DigiXros requirements for each card placed. This is shown on cards using text such as "DigiXros -2: [Shoutmon]×[Ballistamon]×[Dorulumon]×[Starmon s]."

7-2-2-1.text: When performing a DigiXros, the play cost is reduced by the amount shown in the DigiXros requirements for each card placed for the DigiXros. (Example: For DigiXros requirements that read "DigiXros -1: [Shoutmon]×[Ballistamon]," a player can place [Shoutmon] and/or [Ballistamon] cards under the played card, and the play cost of the played card is reduced by 1 for each card placed.)

7-2-2-10.text: An X-card DigiXros is considered to be performed when X cards are placed under the card to be played for the DigiXros. If X cards aren't placed under the card to be played, an X-card DigiXros17 isn't considered to be performed even if the player declares a DigiXros. (Example: If an effect reads "[On Play] <De-Digivolve 1> 1 of your opponent's Digimon, then if DigiXrosing with 2 cards, delete 1 of your opponent's Digimon with a play cost of 5 or less," it will be possible to perform the "if DigiXrosing with 2 cards" and later part of the effect only if 2 cards are placed under the card to be played for the DigiXros.)

7-2-2-11.text: If a card can no longer be played while a DigiXros procedure is being performed, the cards placed under it are trashed.

7-2-2-13.text: Effects that affect playing cards will also affect playing cards for a DigiXros.

7-2-2-2.text: A declaration for a DigiXros is made immediately before paying the play cost. If any effects are triggered when the card would be played, the DigiXros declaration comes after such effects. (Example: In order to perform a DigiXros using a card with both DigiXros requirements and a "when this card would be played" effect, first the effect is resolved, then you declare the DigiXros.)

7-2-2-3.text: You declare the DigiXros at the same time as when you choose the cards to place under the card to be played for the DigiXros. After you have chosen all of the cards to place under the card to be played, place them under that card. Once placed, additional cards to place can't be chosen. (Example: Even if you activate a "when this Digimon would leave the battle area, return 1 yellow Digimon card from this Digimon's digivolution cards to the hand" effect when placing the cards chosen for a DigiXros under the card to be played, the cards returned to the hand by this effect can't be placed under the card to be played for this DigiXros.)

7-2-2-4.text: A player can place any number of the cards specified in the DigiXros requirements for a DigiXros. However, if a DigiXros has been declared, the player can't choose to place 0 cards.

7-2-2-5.text: 1 of each of the cards specified in the DigiXros requirements can be placed for the DigiXros. However, if a DigiXros has the number of cards specified, only up to that number of cards can be placed.

7-2-2-6.text: When cards will be placed under a card from the hand for a DigiXros, that card is to be revealed from the hand at the same time as the declaration for the DigiXros.

7-2-2-7.text: If a DigiXros is used to place a card in the battle area under a card, the placed card is considered to leave the field at that timing.

7-2-2-8.text: When cards placed for a DigiXros are stacked, they are placed in order from top to bottom so that the Digimon shown on the left side of the DigiXros requirements goes on top. If the DigiXros requirements specify the numbers of each card, the player performing the DigiXros chooses the stacking order.

7-2-2-9.text: A DigiXros is considered to be performed when 1 or more cards are placed under the card to be played for the DigiXros. If 0 cards are placed under the card to be played, a DigiXros isn't considered to be performed even if the player declares a DigiXros. (Example: If an effect reads "[On Play] [When Attacking] You may give 1 of your opponent's Digimon <Security A. -1> until the end of their turn. Then, if DigiXrosing, this Digimon gets +3000 DP and <Blocker> until the end of your opponent's turn," it will be possible to perform the "if DigiXrosing" and later part of the effect only if a card is placed under the card to be played for the DigiXros.)

7-2-3.text: The processing for a DigiXros is performed using the following procedure.

7-2-3-1.text: During the play procedure, the player proceeds up to the step where the card to play is revealed, then if any effects trigger upon play, those effects are to be resolved.

7-2-3-2.text: A DigiXros is declared immediately before paying the play cost. At the same time, the desired cards to be placed under the card to be played as specified in the DigiXros requirements are chosen from the cards in the hand and/or battle area.

7-2-3-3.text: The chosen cards are placed under the card to be played. The play cost is reduced by the amount shown in the DigiXros requirements for each card placed for the DigiXros. When paying a play cost, the player pays the cost after any increases or reductions.

7-2-3-4.text: The card is placed on the field and the card playing procedure is resolved.

7-3-1.text: Assembly refers to a rule where a player plays a Digimon card with Assembly requirements, places the specified number of the cards specified in that card's Assembly requirements from their trash under the Digimon card to be played, and the play cost is reduced by the value specified in that card's Assembly requirements. This is shown on cards using text such as "Assembly -6: 4 [Negamon] cards."

7-3-2-1.text: By placing the cards specified in the Assembly requirements under the card to be played, Assembly will reduce the play cost as specified in the Assembly requirements. (Example: For Assembly requirements that read "Assembly -6: 4 [Negamon] cards," a player can use Assembly to place 4 [Negamon] cards under the card to be played, and the play cost will be reduced by 6.)

7-3-2-10.text: Assembly can be performed even when an effect is used to play a Digimon card with Assembly requirements.

7-3-2-2.text: A declaration for Assembly is made immediately before paying the play cost. If any effects are triggered when the card would be played, the Assembly declaration comes after such effects.

7-3-2-3.text: You declare Assembly at the same time as when you choose the cards to place under the card to be played for Assembly. After the player has chosen all of the cards to place under the card to be played, they place them under that card. Once placed, additional cards to place can't be chosen.

7-3-2-4.text: The exact number of cards specified in the Assembly requirements must be placed for the Assembly. A player can't place just some of the specified cards.

7-3-2-5.text: 1 of each of the cards shown in the Assembly requirements can be placed under the card to be played for Assembly. However, if Assembly specifies the number of cards, only that number of cards can be placed.

7-3-2-6.text: When cards placed for Assembly are stacked, they are placed in order from top to bottom so that the card shown on the left side of the Assembly requirements goes on top. If the Assembly requirements specify the same cards or the numbers of each card, the player performing the Assembly chooses the stacking order.

7-3-2-7.text: If no cards are placed under the card to be played, an Assembly isn't considered to be performed even if the player declares an Assembly.

7-3-2-8.text: If a card can no longer be played while the Assembly18 procedure is being performed, the cards placed under it are trashed.

7-3-3.text: The processing for Assembly is performed using the following procedure.

7-3-3-1.text: During the play procedure, the player proceeds up to the step where the card to play is revealed, then if any effects trigger upon play, those effects are to be resolved.

7-3-3-2.text: Declare an Assembly immediately before paying the play cost. At the same time, the cards to be placed under the card to be played as specified in the Assembly requirements are chosen from the cards in the trash.

7-3-3-3.text: The chosen cards are placed under the card to be played. The play cost is reduced by the amount specified in the Assembly requirements. When paying a play cost, the player pays the cost after any increases or reductions.

7-3-3-4.text: The card is placed on the field and the card playing procedure is resolved.

8-1-1.text: Digivolution refers to a rule that allows a player to reveal a Digimon card and stack it on top of their card on the field to change that card. A player can digivolve a card on the field into their Digimon card by paying its cost as part of their main phase actions. (For details, refer to 6-5 "Main Phase")

8-1-2-1.text: When 1 card has multiple digivolution requirements, the player chooses the digivolution requirement for the revealed card. For details, refer to 2-3-6 "Digivolution Requirements")2-3-5

8-1-2-2.text: If ignoring the digivolution requirements when digivolving, the digivolution will occur regardless of the digivolution requirements. Even if a card has digivolution requirements, they aren't referenced. If it doesn't have digivolution requirements, digivolution is still possible.

8-1-2-3.text: A digivolved Digimon carries over its orientation from before the digivolution. (Example: When digivolving a suspended Digimon, the Digimon card stacked on top will also be suspended.)

8-1-2-4.text: Immediate-type effects that trigger when digivolution would occur will trigger immediately after the card is revealed and the card for digivolution is chosen during the digivolution procedure. (For details, refer to 15-8-5 "Immediate-Type Effects")15-8-5

8-1-2-5.text: 1 digivolution can only be performed on 1 Digimon. You can't perform separate digivolutions on multiple cards at the same time.

8-1-2-6.text: If a card can no longer be digivolved after revealing it as part of the procedure for digivolving it, the revealed card is returned to its original location. This isn't considered removal from an area. In addition, the memory doesn't move when a card can't be digivolved because its cost can't be paid.

8-1-2-7.text: Digivolution isn't considered adding to a Digimon's digivolution cards.

8-1-2-8.text: Digivolution is also possible in situations where a draw isn't possible. In such cases, the digivolution processing is performed without drawing a card.

8-1-3.text: The processing for digivolution is performed using the following procedure.

8-1-3-1.text: The player declares a digivolution and reveals 1 Digimon card for the digivolution. 1 digivolution requirement is chosen on the revealed card, then the player chooses 1 of their cards on the field that meets the requirement.

8-1-3-2.text: The digivolution cost specified in the chosen digivolution requirement is paid. (For details, refer to 2-3-6 "Digivolution Requirements")2-3-5

8-1-3-3.text: The player places the Digimon for the digivolution on top of the chosen card, draws 1 card, and the digivolution process is resolved.

8-2-1.text: DNA digivolution is a rule where 1 Digimon card with [DNA Digivolution] is revealed and multiples of a player's cards that meet the revealed card's DNA digivolution requirements are stacked in the order as shown in the requirements, changing the stacked cards and revealed card by digivolving it into 1 new Digimon. This is shown on cards using text such as "[DNA Digivolution] Blue Lv.4 + green Lv.4: Cost 0"

8-2-2-1.text: DNA digivolution differs from standard digivolution in that the cards that become digivolution cards digivolve as different Digimon or Tamers, etc. A DNA digivolved Digimon doesn't carry over the states of the cards that become digivolution cards. Instead, they are treated as follows.

8-2-2-1-1.text: The card placed on top digivolves unsuspended without carrying over the Digimon's orientation from before the digivolution. That Digimon isn't considered to switch from suspended to unsuspended.

8-2-2-1-2.text: All cards that become digivolution cards are considered to be new cards. If a Digimon has a link card from before the digivolution, the link card is trashed immediately before placing the Digimon as a digivolution card.

8-2-2-1-3.text: If a Digimon was attacking before a digivolution, the attacking Digimon is considered to be no longer present. (For details, refer to 11 "Attacking")

8-2-2-1-4.text: If a Digimon was an attack target before a digivolution, the attack target is considered to be no longer present. (For details, refer to 11-2-7 "Attack Targets")

8-2-2-1-5.text: If a Digimon was chosen for an effect or if any effects were applied to it before a digivolution, all those effects end. (For details, refer to 15-13 "Gained Effects")

8-2-2-1-6.text: Any [X Per Turn] uses on a DNA digivolved card will be reset. (For details, refer to 15-14-1 "X Per Turn")

8-2-2-1-7.text: If a Digimon digivolves during the same turn it was played, it loses the information stating that it was played that turn, and it can now attack during that turn.

8-2-2-2.text: When cards placed for DNA digivolution are stacked, they are placed in order from top to bottom so that the Digimon shown on the left side of [DNA Digivolution] goes on top. If the numbers of each card or multiples of a card are specified in [DNA Digivolution], the player performing the DNA digivolution chooses the stacking order.

8-2-2-3.text: The Digimon that will become digivolution cards for a DNA digivolution are placed along with their own digivolution cards in the digivolution cards of the DNA digivolved Digimon. At such times, the stacking order of the digivolution cards can't be changed.

8-2-2-4.text: DNA digivolution can only be performed by an effect that specifically performs DNA digivolution. DNA digivolution can't be performed by an effect that performs standard digivolution.

8-2-2-5.text: Effects that affect digivolution will also affect DNA digivolution. (Example: An effect that reads "[Opponent's Turn] When your opponent's Digimon with no digivolution cards would digivolve, add 1 to the digivolution cost" will also add to the digivolution cost when a Digimon with no digivolution cards would DNA digivolve.)

8-2-3.text: The processing for DNA digivolution is performed using the following procedure.

8-2-3-1.text: The player declares a DNA digivolution and reveals 1 Digimon card for the DNA digivolution. 1 DNA digivolution requirement is chosen on the revealed card, then the player chooses their multiple cards that meet the requirement.

8-2-3-2.text: The digivolution cost specified in the chosen DNA digivolution requirement is paid.

8-2-3-3.text: The cards chosen to become digivolution cards are placed along with their own digivolution cards. The player places the Digimon for the DNA digivolution on top of the stack, draws 1 card, and20 the DNA digivolution process is resolved.

8-3-1.text: Burst digivolve is a rule where a player reveals 1 Digimon card with [Burst Digivolve] and returns 1 of their Tamers from the battle area as specified in the [Burst Digivolve] card's burst digivolve requirements in order to digivolve one of their cards specified in the revealed card's burst digivolve requirements into the revealed card. This is shown on cards using text such as "Burst Digivolve [ShineGreymon]: By returning 1 [Marcus Damon] to the hand, cost 0."

8-3-2-1.text: When digivolution is performed by burst digivolve, as part of the pending processing, the top card of the digivolved Digimon's stack is trashed at the end of the turn it digivolved. However, if there are no stacked cards or that card is not a Digimon, no card is trashed. (For details, refer to 18-1 "Pending Processing")

8-3-2-2.text: Burst digivolve can only be performed by an effect that specifically performs burst digivolve. Burst digivolve can't be performed by an effect that performs standard digivolution.

8-3-2-3.text: Effects that affect digivolution will also affect Burst Digivolve. (Example: An effect that reads "[Opponent's Turn] When your opponent's Digimon with no digivolution cards would digivolve, add 1 to the digivolution cost" will also add to the digivolution cost when a Digimon with no digivolution cards would burst digivolve.)

8-3-3.text: The processing for burst digivolve is performed using the following procedure.

8-3-3-1.text: The player declares a burst digivolve and reveals 1 Digimon card for the burst digivolve. 1 burst digivolution requirement is chosen on the revealed card, then the player chooses one of their cards on the field that meets the requirement.

8-3-3-2.text: The player's Tamer specified in [Burst Digivolve] is returned from the battle area to the hand.

8-3-3-3.text: The digivolution cost specified in the chosen burst digivolve requirement is paid.

8-3-3-4.text: The player places the Digimon for the burst digivolve on top of the chosen card, draws 1 card, and the burst digivolve process is resolved.

8-4-1.text: App fusion is a rule where a player reveals 1 Digimon card with [App Fusion], chooses a pair of linked cards in the battle area from 2 of the specified cards in the revealed card's app fusion digivolution requirements, and stacks the link card of the chosen cards on top of that Digimon, digivolving the stacked cards into the revealed card. This is shown on cards using text such as "[App Fusion] [Gatchmon] & [Navimon] & [Tweetmon]: Cost 0."

8-4-2-1.text: App fusion allows a linked Digimon to digivolve using a combination of 2 different specified cards. (Example: If "[App Fusion] [Gatchmon] & [Navimon] & [Tweetmon]: Cost 0" is specified, a linked Digimon consisting of a combination of 2 cards from among [Gatchmon], [Navimon], and [Tweetmon] can app fuse.)

8-4-2-2.text: App fusion by an effect can only be performed by effects that specifically perform app fusion. App fusion can't be performed by an effect that performs standard digivolution.

8-4-2-3.text: Effects that affect digivolution will also affect app fusion. (Example: An effect that reads "[Opponent's Turn] When your opponent's Digimon with no digivolution cards would digivolve, add 1 to the digivolution cost" will also add to the digivolution cost when a Digimon with no digivolution cards would app fuse.)

8-4-3.text: The processing for app fusion is performed using the following procedure.

8-4-3-1.text: The player declares app fusion and reveals 1 Digimon card to app fuse. 1 app fusion digivolution requirement is chosen on the revealed card, then the player chooses one of their cards in the battle area that meets the requirement.

8-4-3-2.text: The digivolution cost specified in the chosen app fusion digivolution requirement is paid.

8-4-3-3.text: A link card on the chosen card is placed on top of21 that Digimon as specified in the app fusion digivolution requirements. The player places it on top of the Digimon card to app fuse, draws 1 card, and the app fusion process is resolved.

9-1-1.text: Using a card refers to a rule where an Option card's [Main] effect is activated. When using a card, its color requirements must be met. For details, refer to 4-19 "Color Requirements")4-22

9-1-2.text: If an Option card is used, its [Main] effect will activate. Other effects and rule checks don't interrupt the period between use and activation.

9-1-3.text: When using an Option card, if its [Main] effect has conditions, the effect can be activated when the conditions are met. (Example: If an effect reads "[Main] By trashing 1 card in your hand, delete 1 of your opponent's level 6 or lower Digimon. If this effect trashed a card with the [Seven Great Demon Lords] trait, place this card in the battle area," and you trash a card from your hand after using that Option card, you delete 1 of your opponent's level 6 or lower Digimon.)

9-1-4.note: While the used Option's [Main] waits on its hand pick, the Option is in neither the hand, the trash nor the battle area.
9-1-4.text: A used Option card is treated as not being in any area during the period from activation of its 1st [Main] effect until it's been resolved.

9-1-5.note: The used Option is disposed in the step that finishes its [Main] body (drain_effect_queue_inner right after the OptionMain entry; the top of drain_effect_queue when the body's last selection has just resolved), before the rules check and any trigger, and logs a GameEvent::Trash. Both halves green: a 0 DP rule-check deletion's would-be-deleted decision parks with the Option already trashed, and a triggered [On Play]'s decision is the next one (no 'Trash the used Option' TriggerOrder branch); the event log orders the Option's Trash before the rule check's effect and deletion and before the [On Play]'s memory gain (F-ENGINE-EFFECT-USED-OPTION-MAIN-IS-ORDERABLE, G-ENGINE-OPTION-TRASH-NO-EVENT resolved). Proven for a player-used Option only: an Option used by an effect from inside a selection callback can still see a rules check before its trash, and only the last queued [Main] (not the 1st) ends the period; both are recorded as residuals in the F- entry, untested. Update (2026-10-17): both residuals closed -- an Option an effect uses from inside its selection callback is trashed before the rule check its [Main] caused (the disposal gate compares to the deferred-depth baseline the body started under), and an Option with two [Main] effects is trashed after the FIRST, the second resolving afterwards from the trash; hand / deck redirects log GameEvent::CardToHand / CardToDeck.
9-1-5.text: A used Option card is immediately trashed as pending processing as soon as the timing when its 1st [Main] effect has been resolved, unless that Option card is considered to be placed in an area. Other effects and rule checks don't interrupt the period between [Main] effect activation and trashing. (For details, refer to 18-1 "Pending Processing")

9-1-6.text: Immediate-type effects that trigger when a card would be used will trigger immediately after the card is revealed during the use procedure. (For details, refer to 15-8-5 "Immediate-Type Effects")

9-1-7.text: Cards are used 1 at a time. Multiple cards can't be used at the same time.

9-1-8.text: If a card can no longer be used after revealing it as part of the procedure for using it, the revealed card is returned to its original location. This isn't considered removal from an area. In addition, the memory doesn't move when a card can't be used because its cost can't be paid.

9-1-9.text: The processing for using an Option card is performed using the following procedure.

9-1-9-1.text: The player declares use of a card and reveals the Option card to be used.

9-1-9-2.text: The specified use cost is paid. (For details, refer to 2-7 "Use Costs")2-7

9-1-9-3.text: When use of an Option card is resolved, its 1st [Main] effect is activated.
